stories.title: Luka Doncic returns for Lakers; Austin Reaves, Quentin Grimes out vs. Hawks
stories.summary: Luka Doncic returned for the Lakers on Monday at Atlanta, but the team was without Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (sprained finger).
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- The Los Angeles Lakers got Luka Doncic back in the lineup Monday against the Atlanta Hawks but were not at full strength with Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (sprained finger on right hand) both out. Despite being short-handed, the Lakers beat the Hawks 124-114 to improve to 10-2. They are on a six-game winning streak. Reaves scored a season-high 43 points in Sunday's 121-116 win over the Detroit Pistons while Doncic was sidelined because of lower back tightness. Doncic finished with 32 points Monday after scoring 40-plus in four straight games. He leads the league with a 40.1 points-per-game average. Lakers coach JJ Redick said that with Reaves and Grimes sidelined, he planned to give early rotation minutes to rookie Cameron Carr , L.A.'s first-round pick.

stories.title: Jerome scores 27 points as Grizzlies improve to 5-0 on road by routing short-handed Raptors 118-102
stories.summary: — Ty Jerome scored 27 points, Cameron Boozer added 22 and the Memphis Grizzlies improved to 5-0 on the road this season by beating the short-handed Toronto Raptors 118-102 on Monday night.
stories.detailText: TORONTO -- — Ty Jerome scored 27 points, Cameron Boozer added 22 and the Memphis Grizzlies improved to 5-0 on the road this season by beating the short-handed Toronto Raptors 118-102 on Monday night. Memphis is the only NBA team without a road loss this season. They’ve also won at Golden State, Sacramento, Utah and Portland. Jerami Grant scored 17 points and Jaylen Wells had 14 as the Grizzlies snapped a three-game losing streak and won for the fifth time in six trips to Toronto. Boozer had eight rebounds and eight assists. Zach Edey had eight points and nine rebounds in his lone regular-season visit to his hometown. Memphis was without center Isaiah Stewart (right knee) for the second straight game. Grizzlies center Quinten Post left in the first quarter after being elbowed in the face while defending Jamison Battle’s drive to the basket. Jamal Shead had 20 points and 11 assists for the Raptors, who played without three starters. Kawhi Leonard (left knee) missed his sixth straight game, while Scottie Barnes (left groin) and Immanuel Quickley (right hamstring) each sat for the second straight. The Raptors were also without reserve forward Collin Murray-Boyles , who sat out because of an illness. RJ Barrett scored 19 points for Toronto. Battle and Jakob Poeltl each had 18 and Ja’Kobe Walter added 12. The Raptors won their opening two games of the season but haven’t won back-to-back games since. Up next Grizzlies: Host Denver on Wednesday night. Raptors: Host Boston on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Collins puts up 24 points and 10 rebounds as Pistons beat Davis and Wizards, 122-111
stories.summary: — John Collins had 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Detroit Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 122-111 on Monday at Little Caesars Arena.
stories.detailText: DETROIT -- — John Collins had 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Detroit Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 122-111 on Monday at Little Caesars Arena. The Pistons overcame a 44-point, 13-rebound performance from Anthony Davis , who had been a game-time decision because of an ankle issue. Daniss Jenkins finished with 22 points and eight assists after moving into the starting lineup. Jenkins scored a career-high 31 points in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Lakers . Duncan Robinson scored 22 for Detroit. AJ Dybantsa scored 21 points for Washington, which lost its fourth straight. Trae Young had 20 points and seven assists. The Pistons led by 10 at the half and shot 63.2% from the floor in the third quarter. Jenkins had 13 points in the quarter as Detroit extended the lead to 103-87. Cade Cunningham didn't return until midway through the fourth quarter after picking up a fifth personal foul in the third, but the Pistons had built a comfortable 115-99 lead. Davis, who set the scoring record at the Palace of Auburn Hills with a career-high 59 points for the Pelicans in 2016, started the game like he was headed toward breaking Anthony Edwards ' Little Caesars Arena record of 53. He finished with 30 points in the first half on 10 of 11 shooting — making both of his 3-point attempts and 8 of 9 attempts from the free-throw line. But he didn't get much help. Young scored 13 points in the half, but the other three starters combined for 14 points and the bench added just one point. Meanwhile, the Pistons had three starters in double figures — Robinson, Collins and Cunningham — and got 19 points from the reserves. Up next Wizards: At Indiana on Wednesday before hosting Detroit on Thursday. Pistons: At the Washington on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Luka Doncic powers the Lakers past the Hawks, stretching the win streak to 6
stories.summary: — Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- — Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night. Walker Kessler had 21 points and 10 rebounds, and Collin Sexton had 18 points and six assists off the bench. The Lakers were without guard Austin Reeves, who missed the game due to illness one day after scoring 43 points at Detroit. Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 23 points and was 5 of 8 from 3-point range. The Lakers as a team shot 43% from beyond the arc (15 of 35). CJ McCollum led the Hawks with 21 points off the bench. Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 20 points and Oneka Okongwu had 16 for Atlanta, which saw its winning streak end at four games. Dyson Daniels was the primary defender on Doncic, and he also had 10 points, eight assists, four steals and a rare 3-pointer. The Hawks pulled cut the Lakers lead 115-111 on a Daniels bucket with 3:30 to play, but a 6-0 burst by the Los Angeles put the game out of reach. Doncic had a driving layup and an assist during the run. The Lakers built a 20-point lead in the second quarter as they sliced through the Hawks defense repeatedly. Doncic set up teammates with eight first-half assists and Kessler had three easy alley-oop dunks off Sexton drives to the basket. The Hawks recovered late in the half with some improved shooting and cut the deficit to nine at the break. Lakers rookie Cameron Carr had a two-handed dunk in transition in the first quarter for his first career points. Up next Lakers: At Milwaukee on Wednesday night. Hawks: At Chicago on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Hornets humiliate the Cavs 124-112
stories.summary: This is the kind of loss that forces an organizational shakeup.
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 9: James Harden #1 and Evan Mobley #4 of the Cleveland Cavaliers looks on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on November 9, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers , in desperate need of a get-right game, put together one of their worst performances in recent (regular season) memory by getting blown out by the Charlotte Hornets 124-112 on Monday night. The Cavs fall a game under .500 before heading to New York on Wednesday to play the defending champion Knicks on national television. Instead of using tonight’s game as a momentum builder, the Cavs were laughed out of the arena by the woeful Hornets. Cleveland trailed by as many as 33 points against the NBA’s worst offense in Charlotte, a team that was already missing several key players. Grayson Allen (27 points on 8-of-14 shooting) and Naz Reid (25 points, 13 rebounds) thoroughly outplayed Cleveland’s starters, resulting in a 16-point deficit at the half. That ballooned to 27 points at the end of the third quarter, leading to none of the Cavs’ starters returning to the game after that. Jarrett Allen returned to the starting lineup, finishing with 12 points and seven rebounds in 19 minutes. Donovan Mitchell and James Harden had 11 points each and combined to shoot 7-20 from the floor. Harden in particular was disastrous and had some of the worst defensive possessions you will ever see from an NBA player. Evan Mobley had an exceptionally ineffective game, too, with nine points and four turnovers. Harden and Mobley had a combined +/- of -46 tonight, which passes the eye test. Not only did Charlotte’s starters outplay the Cavs, but Cleveland’s backups did too. Craig Porter Jr., Thomas Bryant, Thomas, and Norchad Omier brought the Cavs within eight points late in the fourth quarter before running out of steam. But the reserves showed a lot of heart, and considerably more effort and energy than Cleveland’s starters. The Cavs were out-rebounded 49-32 overall, but didn’t get their first offensive rebound until the third quarter, losing that battle 17-3. Cleveland actually ended up with fewer turnovers and shot better from the field than Charlotte, but the final score didn’t reflect that. This is the type of loss that reverberates through an organization, especially one that is expensive and on a fixed timeline like the Cavs. There is a heightened sense of urgency to right the ship, but Cleveland remains exceptionally inconsistent and underwhelming. Despite quality wins against Minnesota and Philadelphia, the Cavs feel like a team teetering on the edge of the abyss. Losses like tonight’s are what push things over.

stories.title: No Austin Reaves, no problem. First-place Lakers beat Hawks for sixth consecutive win
stories.summary: Luka Doncic finishes with 32 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds and five steals as the Lakers defeat the Atlanta Hawks 124-114 for their sixth straight win.
stories.detailText: Lakers guard Collin Sexton celebrates during the first half of a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night. (Mike Stewart / Associated Press) Austin Reaves took the baton from Luka Doncic when Doncic sat out Sunday, and when the roles were reversed Monday, Doncic passed it to his teammates. Doncic had 32 points and 10 assists in a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks as the Lakers won their sixth game in a row, surviving a short bench and a Hawks comeback. One night after sitting out with low back tightness, Doncic struggled with his shot, but reached double-digit assists with eight rebounds and five steals. Lakers center Walker Kessler had 21 points with 10 rebounds, his sixth double-double in the past seven games, and forward Sandro Mamukelashvili had 23 points and eight rebounds off the bench to help overcome the absences of Reaves and Quentin Grimes . Read more: Austin Reaves steps up in Luka Doncic's absence to lead Lakers over Pistons The Lakers (10-2) didn’t look like a team playing on consecutive nights. They blitzed the Hawks (7-5) with 13 unanswered points and ran up the lead to 20 midway in the second quarter. Guard Collin Sexton and Kessler connected on back-to-back alley-oops during the second quarter to inject life into a shorthanded second unit. Reaves, who scored 43 points in a thrilling win over Detroit on Sunday, didn’t play because of illness. Grimes suffered a sprained finger on his right hand against Detroit, although Lakers coach JJ Redick doesn’t anticipate that the injury will keep the guard sidelined for long. X-rays were negative, Redick said, and Grimes could return as soon as Friday’s game in Milwaukee. With two of their regular ballhandlers out, the Lakers needed to rely on Sexton to take pressure off of Doncic’s offensive responsibilities. Sexton, an Atlanta native playing 15 minutes away from his high school, delivered with eight points and three assists in the second quarter alone. Lakers star Luka Doncic drives between Atlanta's Dyson Daniels, right, and Luguentz Dort in the first quarter Monday. (Kevin C. Cox / Getty Images) Showing his history with Kessler, his former teammate with the Utah Jazz, Sexton expertly navigated the pick-and-roll with the Lakers’ center when Doncic was on the sideline. Sexton hit a three with 4:45 remaining in the fourth to put the Lakers up by seven. The Lakers turned to their two youngest players late. Rookie Cameron Carr earned his first rotation minutes and even started the fourth quarter. Carr, whose father Chris played in the NBA and famously lost the 1997 dunk contest to Kobe Bryant, scored his first NBA points, appropriately, on a dunk. Doncic snatched a pass away from the Hawks and hit Carr on an outlet pass. The 21-year-old rookie gathered for an emphatic, two-handed dunk. The first-round pick had two points and three rebounds. Second-year forward Adou Thiero, who only made his season debut two games ago after struggling with left knee swelling, had two points, two rebounds, an assist and a steal. stories.title: Grayson Allen scores 27, Naz Reid adds 25 as Hornets beat Cavaliers 124-112 to snap 6-game skid
stories.summary: — Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 on Monday night to snap a six-game losing streak.
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 on Monday night to snap a six-game losing streak. Tidjane Salaun added 14 points off the bench and Ryan Kalkbrenner had 15 rebounds for Charlotte, which shot 23 of 46 from 3-point range. Charlotte built a 33-point lead in the third quarter then hung on to win after the Cavaliers cut the lead to 118-110 with four minutes left. Meleek Thomas led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points. The Hornets came into the game ranked second to last in the league in 3-point field goal percentage at 28.8%, but hit 12 of 24 from deep in the first half to build a 16-point halftime lead. Allen, Reid and Salaun combined for 52 of Charlotte’s 69 points before the break. Eager for their first win since Oct. 26, the Hornets stayed hot in the third quarter and extended the lead to 33 with Sion James knocking down three key 3s. He finished with 11. Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson chose to play his reserves the entire fourth quarter even after his team trimmed the lead to single digits. But the Cavaliers couldn't get any closer than eight and Royce O'Neale 's 3 from the right wing with 2:40 left in the game pushed the lead to 13. It was a big win for the Hornets. who played without starters Brandon Miller (hip strain), Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Moussa Diabate (quadriceps). Peyton Watson added 13 points and Jared Allen had 12 for the Cavs. James Harden and Donovan Mitchell each had 11. Up next Cavaliers: At New York on Wednesday night. Hornets: At Phoenix on Thursday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Cooper Flagg breaks down in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich
stories.summary: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg has recently started eating an in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich.
stories.detailText: With a comfortable lead against the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday, Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg headed to the bench for good early in the fourth quarter. He put on his warmups, sat next to teammate Daniel Gafford and watched the Mavericks close out a 130-93 victory. Moments later, the Mavericks' TV broadcast caught Flagg with a small plastic bag in hand, taking out a peanut butter and jelly sandwich and having a bite. "Boy, that looks good right now," former Mavericks guard Derek Harper said on the broadcast. It marked the second consecutive game Flagg enjoyed a peanut butter and jelly sandwich during the action. Last Friday, his in-game meal came during a 112-100 win over the Utah Jazz in which he racked up 21 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Cameras similarly spotted him taking a bite. Flagg followed that up with 25 points, a career-high 12 assists and five rebounds in Sunday's game. Not surprisingly, reporters asked the second-year forward about his in-game snack. He first nodded to the Mavs' strength and medical staff before clarifying that he's trying to put on weight and gain muscle. "So those requirements I got to meet. I'm just trying to stay ahead of it," Flagg said Sunday. "We got another game [Monday]. So just trying to get my calories and stay ahead of it and be ready for another one [Monday]." Flagg said that he prefers smooth peanut butter and grape jelly. He added that he also enjoys sandwiches with peanut butter and banana, while sometimes adding honey. The peanut butter and banana combination was one that Gafford, who sat next to him during the postgame news conference Sunday, couldn't get behind. "That one I understand: peanut butter, banana and honey. But I don't know about just [peanut butter and banana]," Gafford said. Mavericks legend Dirk Nowitzki, who contributes as an analyst on Amazon Prime, spoke about Flagg's sandwich consumption. He explained that sometimes "you need a little sugar hit" to keep it going on the court. Whatever the benefit for Flagg, the Mavericks surely approve of the PB&J. Flagg is in the midst of a potential breakout campaign, averaging 24.0 points, 7.0 assists and 6.6 rebounds heading into Monday's game against the Indiana Pacers . The NBA's obsession with peanut butter and jelly sandwiches dates back to Kevin Garnett and the Boston Celtics in December 2007. Garnett ate one before a game, proceeded to play well, and it became a tradition -- one that has been adopted by other players in the league in the years since. Add Flagg to that list, with a twist: He eats his during the game.

stories.title: Warriors guard Will Richard sidelined by torn ligament in left thumb
stories.summary: Richard has been providing key minutes as both a starter and a reserve as Golden State has won seven straight games since an 0-3 start.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO — Second-year Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard has a torn ligament in his left thumb that will sideline him for an undetermined stretch. The Warriors listed Richard on the injury report Sunday with a torn ulnar collateral ligament and he was out for Monday’s game against New Orleans at Chase Center as the team concludes a six-game homestand. Golden State didn’t have practice or media availability Sunday, so there wasn’t an immediate timetable for Richard’s recovery or a known treatment plan. Richard has been providing key minutes as both a starter and a reserve as Golden State has won seven straight games since an 0-3 start. He made two starts this past week, against Phoenix and Miami. Stephen Curry has credited the Warriors figuring out their roles to grab some momentum after dropping the first three games. “Everybody having an impact, throw Will Richard in there, too, he’s had three straight games really where he’s turned up the energy defensively for us,” Curry said after a 116-113 win over the Suns on Monday. “Defensively he’s just been a pest out there.” The 23-year-old guard was a second-round draft pick last year out of Florida after he led the Gators to a national championship. Richard is averaging 5.1 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.0 assists while shooting 47.5% from the floor and 42.9% from 3-point range. Sacramento Kings forward Keegan Murray dealt with the same injury early last season, underwent surgery and missed the first 15 games.

stories.title: Kobe Bryant No. 8 Lakers jersey fetches huge money at auction
stories.summary: A game-worn, autographed No. 8 Kobe Bryant Los Angeles Lakers jersey is among the highest-selling jerseys from the NBA icon.
stories.detailText: Mamba Mentality continues to draw attention. A game-worn No. 8 Kobe Bryant jersey from the 2003-2004 season sold for $1.83 million at The Realest on Sunday, Nov. 8. This is the highest sale of a non-rookie jersey from the Los Angeles Lakers star before he switched to No. 24. It also lands among the top-five highest public auction sales of Bryant's NBA jerseys. The jersey is autographed and was certified by The Realest's authentication program, which utilizes photo-matching. Its only previous owner purchased the jersey with a certificate of authenticity directly from the Lakers via a charity auction in 2017 before the NBA icon passed away. The jersey is believed to have been worn in 17 games that season – with a record of 16-1, including 8-0 in the playoffs – when the five-time champion starred alongside Shaquille O'Neal. Bryant wore it for his 31-point, 10-assist double-double in Game 5 of the first round to eliminate the Houston Rockets , for his 42-point performance in Game 4 of the conference semifinals against the San Antonio Spurs and in Game 6 of the next series against the top-seeded Minnesota Timberwolves to win the Western Conference finals. The jersey has an NBA Finals patch and is the only No. 8 jersey of Bryant's to come to auction with such a detail. It could not be proven if Bryant wore it the NBA Finals, where the Lakers lost to the Detroit Pistons in five games. The highest-selling Bryant jersey was the one from his NBA debut in 1996. It sold in April of 2025 for $7 million. Bryant played 20 seasons in the NBA all with the Lakers. He was drafted No. 13 overall in the 1996 NBA Draft by the Charlotte Hornets out of Lower Merion High School in Philadelphia and was traded to Los Angeles that day. He won five NBA championships with the Lakers, was named Finals MVP for two of the titles and was named an All-Star 18 times. Bryant died in a helicopter crash in January of 2020 at the age of 41 with his 13-year-old daughter, Gianna. Last month, The Realest auctioned off a Shohei Ohtani jersey from the 2025 Tokyo Series for $2,055,700 . It was the most expensive jersey worn by a baseball player in the 21st century. stories.title: Knicks’ Jalen Brunson earns NBA accolade after great week of play
stories.summary: Looks like he’s fine after all
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND, OH - NOVEMBER 7: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks dribbles the ball during the game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on November 7, 2026 at the Rocket Arena in Cleveland, Ohio. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by David Dow/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Remember when all discussions surrounding Jalen Brunson started and ended with struggling, slow, off, and hangover? Well, you can put those talks to rest. After starting the season with five straight games of shooting 43% or lower and averaging just 22.8PPG on 36.6% shooting, the reigning Finals MVP has turned things around. In the Knicks’ three wins last week in which they outscored opponents 347-292, Brunson averaged a cool 27.7PPG and 6.3APG while shooting 48.3% from the field, 42.9% from three and committing just 0.7 turnovers per game. Those numbers helped Brunson win the Eastern Conference Player of the Week award , something he’s now earned 10 times. Jalen Brunson is Eastern Conference NBA Player of the Week for last week: pic.twitter.com/MCegJ4gmDx — Ian Begley (@IanBegley) November 9, 2026 It does pale in comparison to former Mavericks teammate Luka Doncic’s monstrous stat lines that have headlined the young NBA season. The Slovenian forward led his team to a 4-0 record while averaging an absurd 45PPG, 7.0RPG, and 8.3APG. Mavericks fans may be busy elated over the meteoric rise of Cooper Flagg, and rightfully so. But Brunson and Doncic winning it in the same week (something they also did late last November) just months after the former won a championship has to be another reminder of just how badly the Mavericks messed up. For Knicks fans, though, this was validation for the fans who knew that the captain would eventually turn things around. Much of Brunson’s slow start could be attributed to him just missing shots he often makes. Regardless, there was an odd number of fans, both Knicks and non-Knicks, who wondered if he was coming back to earth. The answer is clearly no. Brunson is back to doing Brunson things, making shots, and running the slowly but surely improving offense while taking care of the ball at an elite level. Karl-Anthony Towns also gets a shout-out. The center, who’s in the midst of playing some of the best basketball of his career, has been on fire and was amongst the nominees that Brunson beat out. Nickel Alexander-Walker, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, and Jaylen Brown were the others who lost out to Brunson.

(Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Golden State Warriors wrap up their six-game homestand tonight against the New Orleans Pelicans, which means Jordan Poole is back at Chase Center wearing a New Orleans jersey and, if the last week is any indication, a warmup top he might never take off. He isn’t on the Pelicans’ injury report . He just sat the entire game in Los Angeles on Sunday with a coach’s decision DNP , and he’s played four games all season, averaging six points on 19 percent shooting. Remember when Poole, James Wiseman and Jonathan Kuminga were supposed to be the Warriors’ future? The two-timelines plan had them growing up next to Steph Curry and Draymond Green and eventually taking the keys. All three are gone. Wiseman is getting about five minutes a night as a backup center in New York. Kuminga is starting in Minnesota and scoring 12.3 points per game. Poole is in the final year of the $123 million extension Golden State gave him, watching from the end of the Pelicans’ bench. Jordan Poole spoke on how he feels about trade rumors during his press conference: pic.twitter.com/p9yaBtyxrb — PooleMuse (@PooleMuse) October 30, 2026 Which is wild, because Poole is a big reason there’s a 2022 banner hanging in this building. He scored 17 a night in that playoff run, and Steve Kerr mentioned it plainly when Poole came back with Washington: “We don’t win that championship without him,” he told ESPN . But that was then, and this is YAXEL. Right now this fan base is losing its mind over a 6-foot-9 rookie who plays like nobody told him he’s a rookie. Yaxel Lendeborg is pulling up off the dribble, crashing the glass and leading fast breaks, and on Nov. 1 he dropped 37 on the Clippers at Chase Center with Curry resting, the most by a Warriors rookie since Curry scored 42 in 2010. Nine games in, the No. 11 pick is at 21.0 points and 7.1 rebounds a night. Yaxel Lendeborg joins Wilt Chamberlain (1959) and Rick Barry (1965) as the only Warriors rookies to ever reach 200+ points through their first 10 career games. pic.twitter.com/eoniOxATUM — Golden State Warriors (@warriors) November 8, 2026 Now rewind to May 14, 2021. Curry sat that night too, and a third-year Poole scored a then-career-high 38 against New Orleans at Chase Center. Something about Curry being out can provide opportunities for young players to showcase their abilities. And yes, Yaxel went to Michigan, too. Poole helped the Wolverines reach the 2018 national title game, and Yaxel helped them win the 2026 one . I keep picturing Draymond Green, Michigan State Spartan to his bones, watching the Warriors crown a second Wolverine as the future in five years and quietly wondering who in the front office keeps a maize-and-blue flag in their desk drawer. And Poole knows first hand how about the Spartan gives tough love lessons. Before anybody hands Yaxel the keys, though, Brandin Podziemski would like a word. Last month the Warriors gave him a five-year, $110 million extension , and he has never been shy about where he sees this going. “When they leave this thing, they got to leave it with somebody,” he told The Athletic last year, talking about Curry and Green trusting him with the franchise . Draymond’s advice at the time was to be careful saying that stuff out loud. I wonder what Poole thought when he heard about a young Warriors guard with a fresh nine-figure extension talking about inheriting the franchise. He’s been there. Jordan Poole returns to the bay tonight 🥹🔥 WELCOME BACK CHAMP pic.twitter.com/J5HJB7qd70 — Warriors Lead (@DubsLead) November 9, 2026 Moses Moody, the one young player from that “two timelines” era still on the roster, is working his way back from patellar tendon surgery and isn’t expected back until at least December, which gives Kerr one more young body to sort out when he does. As for tonight, the Warriors have won seven straight after an 0-3 start, the first team to pull that off since the 1950-51 Boston Celtics . Curry is coming off 41 points in Saturday’s overtime win over Orlando, at 38 years old. The Pelicans are 4-6 and on the second night of a back-to-back after losing 139-123 to the Clippers, and New Orleans is without Yves Missi. Golden State will be without Jimmy Butler, Moody, Will Richard and Kristaps Porzingis, with Gui Santos probable, per the official injury report . Tip is at 7 p.m.

stories.summary: The Lakers will be without Quentin Grimes and possibly Austin Reaves for their clash against the Hawks on Monday.

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images UPDATE: Austin Reaves has been ruled out due to illness for Monday’s contest against the Hawks. He’ll miss his first game of the season. Austin Reaves has been downgraded to out tonight in Atlanta with an illness, the Lakers say — Dave McMenamin (@mcten) November 9, 2026 As predicted, with both Grimes and Reaves out, Cameron Carr will be inserted into the rotation for the first time this season, according to head coach JJ Redick pregame. Cameron Carr will play rotation minutes for the Lakers tonight, JJ Redick says — Dan Woike (@DanWoikeSports) November 9, 2026 Original story follows. After a shorthanded win over the Pistons on Sunday afternoon, the Lakers look set to be shorthanded in a different way on Monday. Ahead of their game against the Hawks, the Lakers released their injury report with three notable changes, including the removal of Luka Dončić but the addition of Austin Reaves and Quentin Grimes. Austin questionable and Grimes is ruled out for tonight. pic.twitter.com/XaqlITWB5a — Raj C. (@RajChipalu) November 9, 2026 Reaves’ illness is legitimate as Dan Woike of The Athletic noted that Reaves told him he had been feeling sick since arriving in Detroit on Saturday. His performance against the Pistons , then, was a flu game on top of being his best game of the season. As for Grimes, he left the game during the second half against the Pistons and did not return. After the contest, head coach JJ Redick did not have a full update on Grimes other than noting that x-rays were negative. Luka would be able to step in if Grimes is the only one missing and the Lakers could largely replicate the rotation from Sunday’s win. If Reaves is also out, though, it could mean Cameron Carr’s first real minutes of the season. Carr made his debut and has played in a pair of blowouts late, but hasn’t played meaningful rotation minutes. If the Lakers are down two guards, it’s likely one of he or Bronny James would be the next person up. The Lakers were able to respond while undermanned on Sunday, though. Even with a shuffling of players, it’ll be interesting to see if the Lakers can make it two for two to kick off the road trip. stories.title: Around the West: Sizing up the conference behind the Lakers
stories.summary: How are the 14 teams currently behind the Lakers faring this season?
stories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - NOVEMBER 4: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs blocks the shot of Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks during the game on November 4, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Los Angeles Lakers have ridden a five-game winning streak to the top of the Western Conference with a 9-2 record. Luka Dončić is playing like the MVP, Austin Reaves looks like a legitimate All-NBA guard and a host of role players, headlined by Walker Kessler , are flourishing. While a favorable schedule has benefitted them to some degree, wins count all the same and the Lakers are largely taking care of business, dismantling lesser teams in comfortable fashion. But Los Angeles is not the lone team out West piling up victories. The four clubs directly behind them have won a combined 23 games in a row, led by the San Antonio Spurs’ eight-game winning streak and the Golden State Warriors’ seven-game winning streak. Early season standings are almost always jumbled, but the West is particularly unforgiving thus far. The Portland Trail Blazers began the weekend atop the conference at 6-1, then dropped a back-to-back set to the now No. 1 and 2 seeds and tumbled to eighth. Moving forward, I’ll regularly provide a snapshot of the Western Conference standings with a brief section on every team to offer a glimpse at the Lakers’ fiercest foes. Net ratings are courtesy of Cleaning the Glass and exclude garbage time. Playoff teams 1. Oklahoma City Thunder: 8-2, plus-8.4 net rating (6th in the NBA) Lakers’ record vs. Thunder: 0-0 Before November even arrived, the Thunder were dealt a trio of serious blows as three starters — Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace — all suffered serious injuries and are out for the foreseeable future. After a couple hiccups following a 4-0 start, they’ve rebounded to rattle off four straight wins. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is carrying the mantle as their engine while Ajay Mitchell instills crucial secondary creation. Rookies Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz have also stepped up amid all the injuries to assimilate themselves and help keep OKC afloat. 2. San Antonio Spurs: 8-2, plus-12.2 net rating (1st) Lakers’ record vs. Spurs: 0-0 The Spurs opened the year with a pair of losses and have since rampaged through the league. During their eight-game winning streak, six of their victories have been by double-digits, including five by 16 or more. They’re the only team currently sitting top five in both offensive (third) and defensive rating (fourth). Victor Wembanyama is a two-way wrecking ball. Dylan Harper, now a starter, and De’Aaron Fox have flourished in complementary roles. Their most pressing worry is Stephon Castle’s slow start. He’s struggled adapting to a greater off-ball role offensively, unable to burn teams from deep or attack the rim as often to draw fouls or finish inside. If he rediscovers his form of last year, they’ll be even more potent. 3. Minnesota Timberwolves: 8-3, plus-12.0 (2nd) Lakers’ record vs. Wolves: 0-0 Despite losing Anthony Edwards two weeks ago, the Timberwolves have won five of seven games — including four straight — in his absence. LaMelo Ball’s wondrous shooting and playmaking have eased everyone else’s burden offensively. Rudy Gobert continues to dominate defensively as a nearly unmatched interior defender. Ayo Dosunmu (18.1 points per game) and Jaden McDaniels (17.0) are stepping up to fill the void left behind by Edwards. The Wolves are rolling. 4. Golden State Warriors: 7-3, plus-3.8 (12th) Lakers’ record vs. Warriors: 1-1 An 0-3 start to the year is already forgotten as Golden State’s gone two weeks without losing. Over that span, they’ve scored impressive wins over the Timberwolves, Lakers, Miami Heat and Denver Nuggets. Stephen Curry is a supernova, averaging 31.3 points on 70.8% true shooting. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has proven himself a versatile front-court scorer — capable of posting up, spacing, rolling and handling — and paired aptly alongside Curry. Role players like Brandin Podziemski, De’Anthony Melton and Georges Niang are prospering. This team looks rejuvenated. STEPH DROPS 41, WARRIORS WIN 7TH IN A ROW! HE TIES OSCAR ROBERTSON FOR THE 8TH-MOST 40-POINT GAMES IN NBA HISTORY 🤯 pic.twitter.com/PjiI7QFI3i — NBA (@NBA) November 8, 2026 5. Houston Rockets: 7-3, plus-11.2 (4th) Lakers’ record vs. Rockets: 0-0 Having lost two straight, the Rockets are in a minor lull after a 5-0 start. They’ve benefited from Fred VanVleet’s return and the arrival of Marcus Smart while Alperen Şengün (21-9-8-1-1, 59% true shooting) is loudly stamping his mark across games. Still a metronome of efficiency, Kevin Durant is averaging his fewest points per game (20.8) since his rookie year on a career-low 23.7% usage rate. Subdued burst and ball-handling have limited his creation in recent years, so he’s mostly a high-level play-finisher these days. It’ll be interesting to see how Houston’s offensive hierarchy and performance shakes out by season’s end. Play-In teams 6. Memphis Grizzlies, 6-3, plus-5.2 (9th) Lakers’ record vs. Grizzlies: 0-0 The Grizzlies are a well-rounded group led by Ty Jerome’s full-fledged breakout. The veteran is averaging 26.6 points, 5.3 assists and 3.4 rebounds per game to power Memphis’ surprising start. Rookie Cameron Boozer’s passing and decision-making have popped but he’s labored mightily to score the ball, shooting 33.9% overall and 35.8% inside the arc. Remedying that means figuring out how to get to his spots without touting an overwhelming strength advantage. If he can become an effective scorer, he’ll instill another valuable dynamic for Memphis. 7. Portland Trail Blazers: 6-3, plus-4.2 (10th) Lakers’ record vs. Blazers: 1-1 Behind an array of complementary ball-handlers, some athletic and physical wing defenders and two imposing rim protectors, the Blazers have built a pretty nifty team. Fouls, turnovers and white-hot midrange shooting are sinking their defense (23rd overall) but they’re second in offensive rating with a multifaceted attack. They’ll hope Ja Morant, who’s currently out with a hamstring strain, can return as quickly as possible to further enhance their dynamic offense. 8. Denver Nuggets: 5-3, plus-2.5 (16th) Lakers’ record vs. Nuggets: 0-0 The Nuggets are still searching to find themselves early in the year, though they have won four of five. Nikola Jokić and Aaron Gordon have hardly looked like the terrifying forces of the past few years while the bench rotation hasn’t established much rhythm. Spencer Jones made his season debut this weekend. He’ll help reinforce the wings. Christian Braun’s off-ball scoring resembles that of 2024-25 rather than 2025-26, which is an encouraging development for Denver. Trevon Brazile and Bryce Hopkins might be nice finds as rotation players. Jamal Murray is humming as a scorer and passer. Matchups with Houston and Memphis this week will help illuminate the Nuggets’ current quality. 9. Dallas Mavericks: 6-4, plus-2.8 (14th) Lakers’ record vs. Mavericks: 0-0 Thus far, the Mavericks’ big swing in hiring Dusty May from the collegiate ranks has paid off. He’s established a movement-heavy offense that punishes gap help with cutting, relocating and snappy passing while utilizing all of the talent in the rotation. Cooper Flagg is averaging 24-7-7-2 and playing like an early All-NBA candidate. Kyrie Irving’s shooting and off-ball instincts have paired snugly next to the Mavs’ budding superstar. Dallas should factor into the postseason conversation all year. COOPER FLAGG DELIVERED WITH EFFICIENCY! 🏀 25 PTS (8-13 FGM) 🏀 5 REB 🏀 12 AST (career-high) 🏀 3 3PM 🏀 28 MIN 🏀 @dallasmavs W He's the first teenager in NBA history to record 25+ PTS, 10+ AST, and 5+ REB in under 30 minutes of playing time 🤯 pic.twitter.com/gT8bxFnkuX — NBA (@NBA) November 9, 2026 Lottery teams 10. New Orleans Pelicans: 4-6, minus-0.5 (18th) Lakers’ record vs. Pelicans: 0-0 Peaks and valleys are the themes of the Pelicans’ first few weeks. They opened 0-4, then ripped off four consecutive wins and followed those up with a two-game losing streak. Jeremiah Fears has improved as a driver and finisher. Saddiq Bey and Trey Murphy III chip in with versatile scoring from the wing spots. New Orleans seems too talented to bottom out but too clunky and incongruent to truly compete for a playoff berth. We’ll likely have a much better read on this team by December with another month of games under its belt. 11. Phoenix Suns: 3-5, minus-7.0 (23rd) Lakers’ record vs. Suns: 0-0 Phoenix’s busy offseason in which it revamped its starting five to land Miles Bridges has not panned out through three weeks. That starting group is disjointed and incompatible, lacking the passing, driving and defense to thrive. Second-year center Khaman Maluach has struggled, though shown some flashes on the offensive glass, as a finisher and defending the rim. Devin Booker is lighting up the nets, averaging 25.3 points on 59.9% true shooting. Two wins in a row, most recently over the Rockets, has helped right the ship a tad. We’ll see if they can keep the good vibes going on Tuesday against the Spurs. 12. Los Angeles Clippers: 2-7, minus-4.0 (19th) Lakers’ record vs. Clippers: 2-0 The Clippers opened the year with a win over the Sacramento Kings before suffering seven straight losses, all of which came against postseason hopefuls or title contenders. Then, they knocked off the Pelicans Sunday night. Darius Garland is scoring and shooting well (55.1% on 2s, 37.1% from deep) but is printing giveaways with 5.1 turnovers per game. Keaton Wagler is knocking down 39% of his triples and showcasing off-kilter craft to take 5.8 free throws each night (.712 free-throw rate) but cannot score inside the arc to save his life (28.1% on 2s). His development is the main priority this season. 13. Sacramento Kings: 1-9, minus-12.4 (27th) Lakers’ record vs. Kings: 1-0 One of four one-win teams this season, the Kings are mostly a mess. Darius Acuff Jr.’s passing and off-the-dribble scoring are among the rare glimmers of positivity. The rookie is averaging 25.9 points and 7.4 assists while showing a real knack operating in ball-screens. Following a tough first four games, he’s also been pretty efficient, tallying 28.8 points and 9.2 assists per game while shooting 51.9% on 2s and 38.3% from deep (58.1% true shooting) over his last six outings. 14. Utah Jazz: 1-9, minus-11.9 (26th) Lakers’ record vs. Lakers: 1-0 It is fitting the West’s most disappointing team will punctuate this week’s debrief. The Jazz entered 2026-27 with genuine aspirations and have catastrophically flopped. They’re on pace for their fewest wins and worst net rating since they began rebuilding in 2022-23. Injuries are a factor. They dearly miss Jusuf Nurkic’s screening and passing — a reliance on him is a blaring alarm bell on its own — and Jaren Jackson Jr. has only played four games. But Utah is too often scattered and stagnant offensively, cannot protect the rim and does not generate turnovers. There’s lots of season left but the Jazz have hardly shown signs they’re nearing a turnaround. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Warriors guard Will Richard out indefinitely with ligament tear in thumb
stories.summary: The Golden State Warriors announced that guard Will Richard is out indefinitely with a torn UCL in his left thumb.

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Golden State Warriors announced some surprising news on the team’s injury report for Monday night’s game against the New Orleans Pelicans. Per the Dubs official release, second-year guard Will Richard is out indefinitely with a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his left thumb. A 2023 study found that NBA players who suffered in-season thumb UCL tears missed on average 7.4 weeks of action (although there was a wide range of outcomes). Kings forward Keegan Murray suffered a similar injury last year and missed the first 15 games of the season. Whether Richard is out for a month, three, or more, head coach Steve Kerr will now have a fourth player on the roster unavailable to him in the rotation. Richard joins Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, and Kristaps Porzingis on the Warriors list of players with prolonged absences. Richard was off to a promising start to his sophomore NBA season prior to the injury, averaging 5.1 points and 1.8 rebounds on 47.5%/42.9%/80.0% shooting in 17.2 minutes per game across 10 games (3 starts). The Warriors acquired Richard on a draft night trade back in 2025, acquiring his rights via the 56th overall pick. Richard had helped Florida win a National Championship in his final collegiate season and quickly made an impression in Golden State, looking like an early steal. Richard exploded for 30 points in his seventh NBA game and quickly became a mainstay in the rotation. However, he never again reached those heights and became a solid role player whose effectiveness ebbed and flowed with his jump shot. Thus far this season, Richard was making his threes, but he was also continuing to show veteran savvy as a backcutter in the Warriors offense. Moreover, he was one of Kerr’s go-to point of attack defenders against quick guards. Golden State already lacked point of attack defense, and the current roster does not have any obvious replacements for that component of Richard’s role. Gary Payton II will likely receive more opportunities with perhaps a few minutes for two-way wing Malevy Leons.

stories.title: Is the greatness of Warriors' Steph Curry being taken for granted?
stories.summary: Stephen Curry is doing unprecedented things for the Golden State Warriors. Is his greatness being took for granted?
stories.detailText: It's rare that a player, especially a point guard, at 38 years of age has been as good as Stephen Curry has been. For nearly two decades, the Golden State Warriors' superstar has wowed spectators, surprised teammates, and even coaches with his ability to take over games with a barrage of jaw-dropping, some head-scratching, heart-shattering shots. Curry is in his 18th season, and what he's accomplished all-time has been nothing short of spectacular to start the year. His latest act featured a 41-point outing in a 126-119 overtime win against the Orlando Magic on Saturday, Nov. 7. He scored 17 of his 41 in the final 2:32 of the fourth quarter and overtime, lifting Golden State to its 7th consecutive win after a 0-3 start. He's averaging 31.3 points per game through his first 8 games of the 2026–27 season. For however long it lasts, just don't take it for granted. Draymond Green doesn't and he's played with Curry since 2012. He tries to make a point to tell him congratulations for anything and everything he accomplishes. "You work so hard to get into a position and then after you do something so many times, people don't even tell you congratulations anymore," Green said. "As human beings, you want to feel that ... so I try to make it a point no matter what he does. ... You want to hear other people acknowledge what you do. So I try to make it a point to never get kind of bored, if you will, of his greatness." Steph Curry continues to dominate Head coach Steve Kerr said Curry looks like he's a 29- or 30-year-old, if he didn't already know his age. He's impressed with everything that goes into the longevity of Curry. "Work ethic, and good genes," Kerr said. "He's been blessed with a body that has held up, but he's also earned that through his strength training, his conditioning, fitness level. It's just off the charts. So remarkable, at 38, to watch him still do what he does." Curry has the most 40-point games (16) for a player age 35 or older. He ranks 19th all-time in points scored with 26,778 career points. Most recently, he became the 14th player in NBA history to accumulate at least 25,000 points, 5,000 rebounds, and 5,000 assists. He's only the third point guard ever to do so, joining Oscar Robertson and Russell Westbrook. Curry knows that as he continues to play the game, he's going to climb all-time stat lines as well. It's a testament to the work he's put in over the years, which he said includes his day-to-day, the off-season, and sleep. Is it a lot? Yes. But Curry appreciates every step of the way. "It does make me super proud of the work that's gone in," Curry said of his 40-point at age 35 or older record. "Especially with some injuries and all of that, but just the idea I can still get to a certain level (and) can kind of feed off of that and especially when it's in a winning fashion ... I appreciate the longevity on that." This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Is the greatness of Warriors' Steph Curry being taken for granted?

stories.title: Pelicans' Zion Williamson to miss first game of 2026-27 season, out for rest vs. Warriors
stories.summary: New Orleans is playing the second of back-to-back games after losing on Sunday to the Clippers.
stories.detailText: Zion Williamson will miss his first game of the 2026-27 season on Monday, sitting out the New Orleans Pelicans' matchup with the Golden State Warriors . Williamson is listed out on the team's injury report due to res t . The Pelicans are playing the second of back-to-back games following Sunday's 139-123 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers . The 139 points allowed were the second-most New Orleans has yielded this season, behind the 141 given up in an overtime defeat to the Denver Nuggets . Facing the Clippers, Williamson scored 25 points, shooting 9 for 9 from the floor, and grabbed four rebounds. In 10 games this season, Williamson has averaged 21 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.2 steals per game. Last season, the 6-foot-6 forward appeared in 62 games, the second-highest total of his career. During his seven NBA seasons, Williamson has missed 278 games. That includes sitting out the entire 2021-22 campaign due to a broken right foot. Injuries and struggles with his conditioning have been an issue since the Pelicans selected him No. 1 overall in the 2019 NBA Draft . New Orleans will be without two of its top four scorers against the Warriors. Trey Murphy III is also out for Monday's game with bilateral patellar tendinopathy. Murphy missed the Pelicans' win over the Utah Jazz last Wednesday for the same reason. He is fourth among New Orleans' scorers, averaging 15.6 points and 4.8 rebounds while shooting 37% on 53 3-point attempts. The Pelicans (4-6) have lost two consecutive games after a four-game winning streak. Meanwhile, the Warriors have won seven in a row after beginning their season 0-3.

Joel Embiid is not listed at all on the injury report for plantar fasciitis management in his right foot. Embiid struggled on the last two games of the Sixers’ most recent road trip, shooting a combined 7-of-28 from the floor in those contests. The Sixers will hope he’s able to snap out of the funk as they take on Jaylen Brown’s old team for the first time this season. There are still some injuries the Sixers are dealing with in the frontcourt. Adem Bona has been ruled out for his third straight game after suffering a cervical spine sprain on Nov. 4 in Detroit. Despite strong play at the backup five from Jabari Walker, Nick Nurse said over the trip that the job is still Bona’s when he returns. Asked Nick Nurse what he saw from Jabari Walker. “Played good. stories.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic receives league honor after explosive week
stories.summary: The NBA formally honored the Lakers superstar for his explosive play last week.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA — The NBA formally honored Luka Dončić for his play last week. The league announced that the Lakers superstar was named the Western Conference Player of the Week for games played for Week 3 of the 2026-27 season, which spanned from Nov. 2-Sunday. Luka Doncic averaged a league-high 45 points in games played last week. NBAE via Getty Images Dončić averaged 45 points, 8.3 assists, 7 rebounds and 1.3 steals in the three games he played in that stretch, with the Lakers going 4-0 in the week. The Slovenian guard scored at least 40 points in each game over the last week. He scored an NBA-season-high 53 points in Friday’s home win over the Portland Trail Blazers . Luka Doncic has won his 20th Player of the Week honor. NBAE via Getty Images Dončić entered Monday’s road matchup against the Hawks having scored at least 40 points in four consecutive games. The weekly honor marks his fifth as a Laker and the 20th such award of his career. Knicks guard Jalen Brunson, who was Dončić’s former teammate in Dallas from 2018-22, won the Eastern Conference Player of the Week. Dončić is averaging a league-best 40.1 points to go with 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.7 steals in 36.0 minutes in nine total games this season. He’s the first player since Wilt Chamberlain (1962-63) to average at least 40 points through his first nine games of a season. Luka Doncic is off to a historic start to the season. stories.title: Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup
stories.summary: The Sixers fell to their second loss of the season on Friday night in Cleveland.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers couldn’t rekindle the magic of their comeback home-opening win over the Cavaliers. They fell Friday night in NBA Cup action, suffering a 119-95 defeat in Cleveland. The Sixers dipped to 8-2 and the Cavs improved to 5-4. The Sixers’ top scorers were Jaylen Brown (20 points), VJ Edgecombe (19 points) and Tyrese Maxey (17). The Cavs got 23 points from Donovan Mitchell and 22 from Evan Mobley. The Sixers’ injured players included center Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain). Cleveland was down big man Jarrett Allen (right knee contusion). Sam Merrill sat out the second half with a right elbow injury. With Friday’s loss, the Sixers are 1-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Their next Cup game is scheduled for Nov. 25 against the Heat. The Sixers will conclude their three-road trip Sunday afternoon against the Bulls. Here are observations on their blowout loss to Cleveland: Nightmare start for Embiid, Sixers After a missed Merrill three-pointer, the Sixers steamed ahead on the fast break and Edgecombe opened the scoring with a slam. The Cavs replied with a 15-0 run kickstarted by six straight Mitchell points. Much like in the Sixers’ Oct. 22 win over Cleveland , they were many levels below their best in the first quarter. The Sixers began 0 for 4 from three-point range, including two LeBron James misses. The Cavs were also the better team in transition and limited the Sixers’ chances to attack in the open floor by taking excellent care of the ball in the early going. Edgecombe was called for his second foul with 7:34 left in the first quarter. Meanwhile, Joel Embiid expressed his frustration about a couple of early no-calls. Embiid’s larger problem was that he couldn’t hit any sort of shot besides free throws. He went 0 for 9 from the floor in the game. The seven-time All-Star finished with six points and seven rebounds. Embiid has had a subpar shooting start to the year, especially from three-point territory — he’s now 3 for 28 (10.7 percent) — but Friday was the kind of extreme night that’s bound to happen here and there over the course of a long season. Of course, it’s notable that Embiid’s been playing through right foot plantar fasciitis and the Sixers have been keeping a close eye on his minutes. We’ll see how the team manages his availability moving forward and whether Embiid is able to bounce back next time out. James didn’t play anywhere near his finest game either. He had eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists and six turnovers. As a team, the Sixers were 36.5 percent from the field and 25 percent beyond the arc. Edgecombe shrugs off foul trouble Jabari Walker rejoined the Sixers’ rotation as the backup center with Bona sidelined. Anfernee Simons, former Cav Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all remained rotation fixtures. With Walker and Caldwell-Pope on the court next to three starters, the Sixers cut their deficit to single digits in the second quarter. Walker threw down a fast-break dunk that cut Cleveland’s lead to 48-41. He gave the Sixers some good defensive possessions when switched on to James Harden and provided his usual physical, high-effort work on the glass. Edgecombe was fantastic in the second, sinking three triples, racking up 15 points and nabbing three steals. Many second-year players would have a tough time finding a rhythm after encountering early foul trouble, but Edgecombe was great as soon as he checked back in and delivered a ton of valuable buckets in the Sixers’ comeback push. Cavs polish it off in 2nd half The Sixers pulled to within 66-63 when Maxey picked a steal and threw a pretty one-handed bounce pass to Edgecombe for a dunk. With Embiid and James offering little as scorers, Brown hit several shots that helped the Sixers stay in the game. After his 30-point performance last time out against the Pistons , Brown reached the 20-point mark for a third consecutive game. Still, the Sixers’ offense never got rolling. The Cavs maintained their lead and extended it late in the third quarter. By early in the fourth, the Sixers trailed by over 20 points. Embiid didn’t play the fourth quarter and logged 25 minutes. He’s had zero made field goals on just one other occasion in his career , back in Nov. 2019 against the Raptors. Even with their tremendous first nine games, the Sixers knew they’d hit speed bumps throughout the year. They’ll try to get back on track Sunday in Chicago.

stories.title: Observations after well-balanced Sixers hold off Bulls
stories.summary: Three Sixers reached the 20-point mark Sunday in a win over the Bulls.
stories.detailText: Observations after well-balanced Sixers hold off Bulls originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Still no losing streaks to speak of for the 2026-27 Sixers. The Sixers earned a 127-121 win Sunday over the Bulls to wrap up a 2-1 road trip. They moved to 9-2 overall and Chicago fell to 1-8. Every Sixers starter scored in double figures. Three reached the 20-point mark in Jaylen Brown (29 points), Tyrese Maxey (27 points) and LeBron James (22). Joel Embiid had 18 points and 10 rebounds. Josh Giddey posted 19 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds for the Bulls. The Sixers were without Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Bulls’ absences included Norman Powell (right shoulder inflammation/soreness) and Zach Collins (respiratory illness). Next on the Sixers’ schedule is a home game Tuesday night vs. the Celtics. Here are observations on their win over Chicago: Embiid sees one go down Following his 0-for-9 night Friday in the Sixers’ loss to the Cavaliers , Embiid did not snap right back into form. He was well short on his first shot attempt, a wide-open three-pointer. Embiid then failed to score in the post over Jalen Smith. Embiid got a field goal to go at the 6:42 mark of the first quarter when he tipped in his own miss. However, Smith canned a three on the ensuing possession to give Chicago a 23-16 lead. James committed two early turnovers, although he did sink a corner three-pointer during a fast-paced first quarter. VJ Edgecombe added two long-range jumpers in the first. Entering Sunday, the Sixers’ minus-9.6 net rating in the first quarter ranked 27th in the NBA. They managed to hold a one-point lead in Chicago after the first. Walker, Sixers shine on the boards The Sixers’ offensive rebounding was their greatest strength in the first quarter. They poured in 17 second-chance points. Embiid had four offensive boards in the opening frame. Jabari Walker assumed backup center duties for the second straight game without Bona. He picked up where Embiid left off on the glass, grabbing seven rebounds (three offensive) in a great first stint. Though he’s undersized in the height department for an NBA center at 6-foot-7, Walker has plenty of rebounding tools. He’s listed at a strong 237 pounds, doesn’t mind contact whatsoever, hunts the ball, and has a knack for winning contested boards. Walker showed all of that Sunday. Very hard to overstate how well he rebounded. Sixers hold off Bulls in final minutes The Sixers’ first-shot offense also had many bright moments in the second quarter. James got rolling on his way to a 16-point first half, Embiid made a couple of mid-range jumpers, and Maxey hit two free throws put the Sixers up 60-50 late in the second period. Chicago evened the game at 68-all early in the third quarter on a Matas Buzelis three, but the Bulls couldn’t sustain that run. The Bulls’ defense continued to look like one of the worst in the NBA and the Sixers’ well-balanced offense kept the scoreboard moving. Brown nailed a turnaround jumper to give his team a double-digit lead. Walker knocked down a top-of-the-key triple to extend the Sixers’ advantage to 12 points. The Sixers had two apparent injury scares in the second half. Brown limped to the sideline with 6:55 to go in the third quarter, but he stayed in the game. Edgecombe headed to the locker room after subbing out at the 9:08 mark of the fourth quarter. He returned to the Sixers’ bench and ultimately returned for a final stint. On the floor, the Sixers couldn’t ease to victory. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson trimmed Chicago’s deficit to 116-113 by draining a three. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse called timeout. The Sixers were efficient enough in the half court down the stretch. Embiid made a put-back hoop and a pair of free throws. Maxey drilled a side-step three-ball after a wraparound feed from James. The Sixers converted their clutch free throws and secured a winning road trip.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.summary: Warriors embracing the Bad Boy role
stories.detailText: Yaxel Lendeborg calls for the Warriors to emulate the Bad Boy Pistons. The Golden State Warriors have played 10 games this season, and rookie phenom Yaxel Lendeborg has given the team a new identity. “Y’all ever heard of the Bad Boy Pistons? Yeah. That’s damn near us,” Lendeborg said. Lendeborg was seen reacting to a second-quarter scuffle between the Warriors and Magic on Saturday night. Yaxel Lendeborg reacts to FlightReacts reacting to the scuffle between Georges Niang and Wendell Carter Jr. and makes a declaration: “We finna be the remodeled Bad Boy Pistons, you feel me. We all— Yeah it’s just been too much going on bro. I feel like there’s 10 ejections in… pic.twitter.com/XqHZoUYPxQ — Yaxel LendeBeast (Loyalist) (@Gmzeroog) November 9, 2026 Wendell Carter Jr. and Georges Niang get into a scuffle in the second quarter of Saturday’s game. AP Photo/Justine Willard The scuffle ignited near the 9:17 mark of the quarter when Georges Niang was seen pushing Wendell Carter Jr. off of him after Tristan Da Silva passed a ball over Draymond Green’s head. During the play, Niang was seen reaching into Carter Jr.’s groin area, and he immediately turned around, and the two started grabbing each other’s jerseys and exchanging words with one another. The tussle caused the players on the court to stop what they were doing and immediately try to separate them from each other. Green, who’s never been shy to tell an opposing player his true feelings, was seen at the front lines of the scuffle and started grabbing Carter Jr.’s jersey and tossed in a few of his own words. Yaxel Lendeborg compares Warriors attitude to the Bad Boy Pistons. AP Photo/Justine Willard “Draymond’s like Ben Wallace, he just don’t be dunking that s—t. You know what I’m saying?” Lendeborg said. Lendeborg then checked history knowledge asking, “If that was the bad boy Pistons era?” “All I know is, that’s us. We finna be the remodeled Bad Boy Pistons.” The rookie might need to brush up on his NBA history. No, Ben Wallace was not a member of the Bad Boy Pistons teams of the 1980s. But they were very physical, en route to winning a championship of their own. Green is the only player on the Warriors to be ejected from a game this season . But Lendeborg said he believes this year’s team has at least “10 ejections in our nearby future.” “I think my boy Dray got two more in him. I feel like I might have two in me. Two in total though cause I’m a rookie; I can’t do this crazy stuff,” Lendeborg said. Draymond Green covering Wendell Carter Jr. on Saturday night. NBAE via Getty Images Lendeborg went on to say that he believes Graham Ike will have “three to four total,” and that he thinks Niang won’t receive an ejection but will have a couple of technical fouls this season. The Warriors went on to win the game, 126-119, as Curry scored 41 points, making it the second time this season he’s scored over 40 points.

(Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to the Game Thread. Veterans of the Game Thread know how we do things around here, but for all you newbies we have a few rules. Our community guidelines apply and basically say be cool, no personal attacks, don’t troll and don’t swear too much. The Spurs are on an eight game winning streak, and they played their most dominant game of the season on Saturday night, running the Trail Blazers out of their home gym 125-103, in a game that wasn’t as close as the final score seemed to indicate. They play the third game of their current four game road trip in Phoenix tonight, and finish up on Wednesday night against the Bulls in Chicago. The Spurs are mostly healthy, although Devin Vassell is listed as questionable for tonight’s game with left adductor tightness. This is the kind of injury that could linger, and San Antonio might let him take a little time off to get fully recovered before he re-enters the lineup. Speaking of guys who are taking time to recover, Tobias Harris has missed the entire preseason and all 10 games of the regular season so far with a calf strain. It would be really great if there would be an update on when he’s expected to return to the lineup, although with the team playing as well as it is now, there’s not a lot of urgency in bringing back online right away. Calf problems are scary, and I don’t have any complaints about making sure he’s fully recovered before he plays in a game, but an actual estimated date for his return would relieve my anxiety. The Suns have been a little disappointing so far this season, with a 3-5 record so far which has them at a way-too-early 12th place in the western conference standings. They defeated the Rockets on Saturday night, and they can beat anyone on a given night with their shooting and scrappy defense. Scrappy 1 is the definition of Dillon Brooks, who always plays a mental game against the opponents in addition to his improved shooting. If he’s not successful in distracting the opponents with his various antics, he’s less effective as a defender, and the Spurs seem to be more capable of handling their emotions on the court this season so far than they did last season. If Vassell can’t play, the Spurs may have to go a little further into their bench rotation tonight, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing. It will be interesting to see who draws the Devin Booker assignment tonight on defense. [Probably Castle] As always, GO SPURS GO! Lets go Spurs, and Reed must dominate Khaman. teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - NOVEMBER 2: Devin Vassell #24 of the San Antonio Spurs looks on during the game against the Utah Jazz on November 2, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images In a very young 2026-27 NBA season that has been rife with injuries, the Spurs have mostly managed to stay above the fray, with Tobias Harris being the only rotation player to miss time with a strained calf suffered in training camp. (And even without him, the Spurs still have the same team that made the NBA Finals.) Tonight will be the first time they are missing a main rotation player, with starting wing Devin Vassell initially listed as questionable before being ruled out against the Suns with adductor tightness. The #Spurs have officially ruled Devin Vassell OUT vs. Suns. #PorVida https://t.co/MPAEQR9ijS — Matt Guzman (@mattgzman) November 9, 2026 Vassell joins Harris and Jayden Quaintance (knee surgery) on the injury report. Two-way players Ja’Kobi Gillespie and Maliq Brown are also away from the team with the Austin Spurs. Just like last season, Vassell has been an integral part of the Spurs’ starting line-up not by putting up big numbers, but by being a steadying presence and reliable relief valve who can get a shot up in the midrange when things break down on offense. He has also been solid on defense despite often having to defend taller players while playing next to the guard trio. This will mark the first time this season the Spurs will have to change the starting line-up. The safe assumption for his replacement would be Julian Champagnie, who was the Spurs starting power forward last season before moving to a bench role this season with Dylan Harper joining the starters. Hopefully Vassell’s injury is nothing serious and he will return soon (the fact that he was initially questionable suggests it likely isn’t serious, but adductors can be stubborn). There has been no timeline offered for Harris’ potential return, although Mitch Johnson has stated that they are being “very methodical” about it, especially considering the Spurs’ fast pace. With an exponential rise in ruptured Achilles associated with playing on sore calves in recent years, who can blame them?
