Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Adam Hagy/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Welcome to Week in Review: a Monday feature that looks back at the week that was for the San Antonio Spurs , takes a look at the week ahead, and more. Enjoy! Week 2 : After a rough opening week of the season, the Spurs took advantage of an easy schedule against the sinking Kings and Jazz and injured Timberwolves to get right again, going undefeated with Victor Wembanyama absolutely dominating by averaging 36 points per game to win Western Conference Player of the Week . Week 3: 4-0 (8-2, 3rd in West ) 119-97 win vs. Utah Jazz It was a rare game where Wemby was not hot, with just 12 points 5-15 shooting, but the Spurs didn’t need him to be in another match-up against the lowly Jazz. He deferred to the hot hands, and they used a balanced attack with all five starters plus Harrison Barnes and Keldon Johnson scoring in double figures, as well as dominant first and third quarters to put the game away early. 112-111 win vs. Dallas Mavericks Unlike the week prior, the Mavericks had Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving available this time, and the match-up lived up to the hype. The Spurs dominated the first half and led by as much as 19, but their inability to protect big leads reared its ugly head again as it completely evaporate in the second half, not helped by the Spurs being ice-cold from three (5-36). But, Wemby once again proved he’s on another tier this season with a historic 53-point, 24-rebound, 8-block night to rescue his team from the jaws of defeat (although it would have been easier had he made his last 4 free throws). 124-109 win at Sacramento Kings (NBA Emirates Cup) In their first Tournament game of the the season, the Spurs made quick work of the cellar-dwelling Kings on the first night of a back-to-back to allow their players to rest in a game that wasn’t as close as the final score indicates (although point-differential does matter in the Cup standings, and the Warriors now lead the group thanks to a 17-point win). Wemby again dominated, with 30 points and 14 rebounds in a quick 26 minutes of work. 125-103 win at Portland Trail Blazers After a sluggish first half featuring two teams on a back-to-back, poor shooting and a heavy whistle (for a total of 41 first-half free throws), the Spurs exploded in the second half against their first-round opponents from last season. Another dominant Wemby game and 17 threes helped the Spurs get out to a 30-point lead in the third quarter, leaving the Portland crowd in stunned silence and heading for the exists early. Power Rankings John Schuhmann, NBA.com — 1 (last week: 4) OffRtg: 117.2 (5) DefRtg: 107.1 (5) NetRtg: +10.1 (3) The Spurs’ winning streak is at eight games, over which they’ve ranked in the top three on both ends of the floor. They’re 8-2 for the second straight season, though they have a better point differential than they had through 10 games last year. Two takeaways 1. Victor Wembanyama scored 52 points (adding 24 rebounds and eight blocks) against the Mavs on Wednesday … with a broken jump shot. After that game, he was 7-for-29 (24%) from mid-range and 12-for-50 (24%) from beyond the arc. But he scored 45 of those 52 points in the restricted area (13-for-16) or at the free throw line (19-for-23), and he may have found his shooting stroke over the weekend. He wasn’t as dominant inside, but made seven of his 12 3-point attempts in Sacramento and Portland. 2. The Spurs’ starting lineup still doesn’t play a ton of minutes; at 10.5 minutes per game, it ranks 13th among lineups that have played at least five games together. It was also outscored by the Kings on Friday. But it’s allowed just 85.8 points per 100 possessions, the best mark among the 22 lineups that have played at least 50 total minutes, and it’s been much better offensively (114.9 scored per 100) than the Spurs were when De’Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle shared the floor last season. Coming up: The Spurs had the league’s best interconference record last season, going 26-4 in regular-season games (that counted in the standings) against the East. Their first interconference game this season is Wednesday in Chicago, the end of a four-game trip. Law Murray, The Athletic — 1 (last week: 4) The slate has been favorable, but the Spurs are doing what they need to do, and that’s win the games and progress accordingly. On that front, Victor Wembanyama is back to reinventing stat lines, so that’s cool. What is more meaningful is that the Spurs might just wind up keeping this starting lineup that features all four of De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell. It’s been working out nicely, with the Spurs outscoring foes by 69 points in the 105 minutes that the five-man starting lineup has been out there together. The three-man lineup of Fox, Castle and Harper specifically has seen the Spurs outscore opponents by 72 points in 113 minutes, with Wembanyama being out there for all of that time. Tobias Harris (calf) will undoubtedly need a ramping-up period, so he isn’t guaranteed a starting role when he gets healthy. Fox has been efficient, Harper has kept turnovers down and Castle has launched more 3s than ever. The Spurs have Wembanyama, and he more than makes up for the lack of fit perfection when it comes to his co-starters. Kurt Helin, NBC Sports — 2 (last week: 7) Unexpected standout: Julian Champagnie. He’s not really an unexpected standout, but is there one on a high-profile team that was in the NBA Finals last June? When Mitch Johnson decided to start three guards — De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, and Dylan Harper — Julian Champagnie was the odd man out and got pushed to the bench. He’s handling it like a pro, and he’s still producing, shooting 42% from 3, giving them almost 10 points a night, and defending well. Brett Siegel, Clutch Points — 2 (last week: 4) Since dropping the first two games of the season, the San Antonio Spurs have rattled off eight straight wins, the longest active win streak in the NBA. However, the combined record of the teams they played during this eight-game span is just 20-26 overall, with six of these wins coming against Dallas, Sacramento, and Utah. Victor Wembanyama has been on a tear lately, averaging 30.8 points, 14.0 rebounds, and 3.5 blocks per game while shooting 54.1 percent from the floor over the last week. In the Spurs’ 112-111 win over the Mavs on Wednesday night, Wembanyama recorded 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks. Aside from recording career highs in points and rebounds against Dallas, Wemby joined Bob McAdoo as the only other player since 1973 to have at least 50 points, 20 rebounds, and five blocks in a single game. Wembanyama has posted MVP-like numbers and carried the Spurs to the No. 2 spot in the NBA power rankings. Coming up Mon. 11/9 at Phoenix Suns (8:00 PM CT) Wed. 11/11 at Chicago Bulls (7:00 PM CT) Fri. 11/13 vs. Golden State Warriors (Emirates Cup, 8:30 PM CT) Sun. 11/15 at Utah Jazz (4:00 PM CT) (After 12 of the Spurs’ first 20 games are 8:00 tip-off times or later, I’m looking forward to the Nov. 29 – Jan. 17 stretch, when NONE of them are later than 7:00. My sleep schedule thanks you, NBA.) Prediction: 4-0 — I doubted and got burned last week (although the Spurs almost made me right with that Dallas game), but I fully believe they’re back now. The only game that should present a challenge (if they keep playing the way they are and don’t relax) is the Warriors, with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg bringing new life to the twilight years of Steph Curry and Draymond Green’s careers. It will likely be a must-win game if the Spurs want to advance in the In-Season Tournament again. (Oh, and if you aren’t tired of the Jazz yet, here they are AGAIN.)

stories.title: Source: Pats' Rhamondre Stevenson expected to miss time with knee tendon issue
stories.summary: Patriots top running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots top running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The injury is to the back of Stevenson's knee and is expected to keep him out the next few weeks, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Stevenson sustained the injury late in the third quarter of the Patriots' blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, when he was twisted down on a 6-yard reception. The Patriots trailed 42-14 at the time. With No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson missing the past two games because of an illness, the Patriots could be down to their third and fourth options -- Corey Kiner and Lan Larison , respectively -- for Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions in Munich. New England also has running back Terrell Jennings on the practice squad. The 5-4 Patriots are scheduled to travel to Munich late Wednesday and then have their bye week after the game. Stevenson has played 65% of the offensive snaps this season, totaling 399 yards on 102 carries (3.9 avg.) and two touchdowns. He has added 26 receptions for 258 yards and two touchdowns. Coach Mike Vrabel noted his excellence in pass protection as a key for the offense. Kiner, whom the Patriots acquired in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals on Aug. 29, could get an increased workload. He has played 13% of the offensive snaps, totaling 244 yards on 50 carries (4.9 avg.). "Corey is working extremely hard and has done a really nice job," Vrabel said earlier Monday, noting that his blitz pickup will be an important area to continue to grow.

stories.title: Monday Night Football: Bills lead Vikings 10-6 at halftime
stories.summary: Josh Allen threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds left in the first half for the halftime lead.
stories.detailText: So much for Carson Wentz stealing Kyler Murray's job. The Vikings offense looks a lot like it has most of the season. The Vikings are struggling to gain yards and score points Monday night against the Bills, who are struggling almost as much against the Minnesota defense. Buffalo leads 10-6 at halftime. The Vikings' first four drives went three plays or less. Their first field goal — a 43-yard kick by Will Reichard — came on a four-play, 9-yard drive after a Bills' punt out of their own end zone. Reichard added a 53-yarder with 5 seconds left in the half, completing a seven-play, 46-yard drive. Two replay decisions went the Bills' way in the first half: 1. Carson Wentz threw a lateral to Justin Jefferson that hit the ground and was covered by Bills defensive lineman Greg Rousseau at the Minnesota 44. Joe Brady challenged the on-field ruling of an incompletion, and replay reversed it to a fumble. The Bills got a 39-yard Tyler Bass field goal out of it. 2. Josh Allen was sacked by Andrew Van Ginkel at the Buffalo 2 and fumbled. Replay, though, showed Allen's knee was on the ground before Van Ginkel knocked the ball loose. The Bills outgained the Vikings 143 to 86 despite three sacks of Allen, who is 13-of-20 for 122 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds left in the first half after rolling to his right to buy time. It was Latu's first career touchdown. Allen was 6-for-6 on the eight-play, 80-yard touchdown drive. James Cook has 15 carries for only 33 yards. Wentz is 7-of-17 for 75 yards, with Jefferson catching two for 39. Aaron Jones has three rushes for 10 yards.

stories.title: The Rams need Matthew Stafford to play like an MVP
stories.summary: The Rams need Matthew Stafford more than ever. Will he deliver?
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams are 5-4 and still in the NFC playoff picture, but the version of Matthew Stafford they have gotten through nine weeks is not the one that carried them last season. Stafford currently has 16 touchdowns and nine interceptions with a 90.6 passer rating. That is functional. It’s nowhere near “MVP” level. Last year Stafford was manufacturing big-time throws and taking care of the football. He has always been prone to mistakes. But this year has reached a higher frequency and there is less of the good to offset. The gap is evident in the efficiency metrics that separate good from elite. Stafford’s big-time throw rate has cratered from 7.7% to roughly 3% this year. His Pro Football Focus (PFF) offensive grade sits in the upper 60’s, good for no better than 20th among qualified quarterbacks. That is not the profile of a player who is elevating the offense around him. It’s the mark of someone who is mostly managing a system, if not part of the problem. The distinction matters because the supporting cast has not been built to absorb a decline in quarterback play. The Rams spent all offseason retooling their defense. The tradeoff brought minimal reinforcements on offense. Puka Nacua, who will now miss at least the next four games , has been asked to handle an outsized share of targets and production. Even when Nacua is available, the rest of the skill players have failed to consistently generate explosive plays. The run game has taken a step forward in stretches. The offense overall has no chance without it. The defense is better. The offense is far from it. On a net basis, the Rams are a worse team. The Rams need Stafford to be the engine in life without Nacua. The last two games against poor competition demonstrate this offense’s current struggles. In two wins, Stafford combined for 385 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. The Rams won both games. It did so without Stafford producing at the level that turns close battles into comfortable victories. That’s good enough against the lowly Chargers and Commanders. It won’t get the job done in a few weeks against the Green Bay Packers. It’s worth noting that Stafford is also managing an elbow issue that has required regular icing and maintenance. The Rams have downplayed the issue, but it landed the quarterback on the injury report last week. Stafford’s decline, although evident, does not require a dramatic injury narrative in order to explain. What is more concerning is the combination of workload, age, and a lesser supporting cast. The margin for error is gone because a lot of the high-end outcomes have disappeared. Last year’s version of Stafford was capable of overcoming some of these constraints. The 2026 quarterback has not shown the same capacity at any point. The Rams do not need Stafford to replicate his MVP stat line. They do need him to reclaim enough of his efficiency and decision-making that defined last season in order to raise the offense’s floor. Doing so requires fewer mistakes, more big-time throws, and production in the deep area of the field. We’ve seen Stafford carry the Rams against all odds before. He pushed young and unproven rosters to the playoffs in 2023 and 2024. The 2026 defense is better than those iterations. Even if the offensive talent is lesser, the team can likely get by scoring fewer points. If Matthew Stafford is truly the MVP, he will rise beyond the injury adversity to help the Rams reach the playoffs and keep their Super Bowl hopes alive. His team needs him more than ever.

stories.title: Could the Jordan Davis trade suggest Eagles are preparing for a new defensive coordinator?
stories.summary: Reactions to the Jordan Davis trade are generally positive for the Eagles, and could also be pointing at even bigger changes.
stories.detailText: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The general consensus is that Howie Roseman won yet another trade, this time managing to get a first and second round pick from the Jaguars for Jordan Davis . As the team racks up draft capital over the next three years , another question is emerging from Davis being traded — could this move imply a new regime for the defense? Specifically, could the move indicate there’s potential for Jim Schwartz to return to Philly? According to Eagles beat reporter Jeff McLane , the team had privately reached out to Jim Schwartz earlier in the year when DC Vic Fangio was contemplating retirement. Moving on from Davis could indicate Fangio is once again considering walking away, and Schwartz’s scheme and personnel needs may already be impacting the Eagles’ roster-building decisions. Even former Eagles legend Brandon Graham spoke about the possibility of Schwartz returning to Philly on the PHLY post-game show — right next to BGN’s Brandon Lee Gowton —, saying that they have the guys his former DC would be able to maximize. BG on the possibility of Jim Schwartz returning to Philadelphia as DC next season if Vic Fangio retires: "I feel like we got Jim Schwartz type of personnel.. Who knows what Vic is going to do next year? I wouldn't be surprised if Schwartz is back." pic.twitter.com/i5ZKpQBQ60 — PHLY Eagles (@PHLY_Eagles) November 8, 2026 There hasn’t been anything to suggest that the Eagles would move on from Vic Fangio unless the legendary defensive coordinator decides to retire, but if he’s given the team any indication that’s his plan, they might be planning for a future with a familiar face. stories.title: A 'confident' C.J. Stroud soaks in five-TD day against Chargers
stories.summary: Stroud matched his career high with five TD passes and added 384 passing yards in the win.
stories.detailText: HOUSTON -- C.J. Stroud 's five-touchdown performance against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday punctuated a hot start for the Houston Texans ' quarterback. Stroud & Co. were dominant in their 44-22 win , as he tied a career high in passing touchdowns to go with 384 yards passing, tied for his second most in a game. Stroud promised himself to "enjoy" his Week 9 performance rather than immediately moving on. "I beat myself up a lot when I don't do great, so I'm going to enjoy this and celebrate with my friends, family and teammates because I know what it feels like to throw a couple interceptions," Stroud said. "So, you need to be positive towards yourself. Something that playing the quarterback position has taught me about life is that everyone could view you one way, but all that matters is how God views you and how you view yourself, so I'm grateful that God has allowed me to have some tough skin and be able to push through some tough times. "Days like this come from being on the other side when you're not playing so great." The Texans' 3-5 record isn't because of poor quarterback play. Through eight games, Stroud has had his strongest start to a season. He has completed 64.2% of his throws for 2,251 yards, 16 touchdowns with only two interceptions, while posting a 104.8 passer rating, and he's on pace for career highs in passing yards and touchdowns. Coach DeMeco Ryans said the fuel for Stroud's high-level performance is "confidence." "You see the growth, you see the maturity in C.J.," Ryans said. "He's a top quarterback in this league because of that, because of his steadiness in the pocket, his resolve, his great energy all day. And he's having a phenomenal year, phenomenal year, and he's definitely deserving of all the recognition that he should get." Against the Chargers, Stroud spread the ball to all of his playmakers -- with receivers Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell each going over 100 yards. Dell finished with 105 yards and a touchdown in only his second game since missing 25 straight after sustaining multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in December 2024. Boutte, whom Houston acquired during the late stages of training camp, had 125 receiving yards with two touchdowns, marking his first outing of the season with at least 100 yards. "It's fun to watch, fun to watch him spin it," Ryans said. "He's thrown it to a lot of different people, which is what I'm most proud of. Everybody's getting the touch, and the guys are showing up and capitalizing on the opportunities that they do get." The Texans' offense ranks 11th in yards (356.5) and ninth in points per game (26.1), and a majority of that production is from their quarterback, who's back to playing how he was during his historic rookie season in 2023. "I'm getting more opportunities, and I'm taking advantage of them," Stroud said. "I think our receivers are doing a great job of blocking their tails off, and our run game is opening up now. It all has to do with a little of everything, but I'm really just grateful that I'm on this team, playing for this city and able to play this great game."

stories.title: Can the Rams really add a receiver to replace Puka Nacua?
stories.summary: The Rams cannot replace Nacua. May go with the receiving group they have, injuries and all
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams will be without Puka Nacua for at least four weeks , and with the Tuesday’s trade deadline approaching, should the Rams make a big-time trade for a wide receiver? Whether they do or not, there is no replacing Nacua, who’s carried the offensive passing game since the Rams lost Davante Adams, who’s also on IR. If the Rams could make a blockbuster (or any) trade to save 2026, they would, but that may not be an option as the NFL trade period comes to its close. The Rams may choose to go with the group they have, injuries and all, and if they do, then they’ll need to play better. Change for the sake of change doesn’t guarantee success. Though it could be naive of McVay to not make major changes on offense this season, the group of pass catchers we’ve seen may be the group going forward as the Rams wait for guys to get healthy. Waiting for guys to get healthy has been a theme for the L.A. Rams this year. Who could the Rams add at receiver? L.A. has been rumored or speculated as linked to potentially trading for receivers like Josh Downs , Brian Thomas Jr. Stefon Diggs , George Pickens and more. Would any of these receivers do what Nacua does for L.A.’s offense? The run after catch, the physicality, maybe. The relationship he’s s built with Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford and the offense? Can any of the names above fill in well enough for both Nacua and Adams to make a trade worthwhile? The Rams would have to make the trade to find out. Can the Rams trade for a receiver who boosts the offense? Yes. They could also trade for a receiver who struggles to connect and build chemistry with Stafford as L.A.’s veteran quarterback is struggling currently with receivers like Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Players Stafford has worked with for years. Trading for a receiver like Thomas Jr. is splashy, but would he and Stafford work well together? Does he fit McVay’s scheme? Would a player like Pickens fit McVay’s culture? Are those receivers worth the Rams sending draft capital for? A trade does not guarantee the Rams a playoff spot Are there any receivers available for the Rams to get going into Week 10 that truly increase their odds at a playoff spot? Going into their 10th game of the year, the Rams sit at 9th in the NFC playoff picture , below the Seattle Seahawks. Below the entire NFC North. Well below the 49ers who sit atop the NFC. Injury is playing a role in the Rams struggles, but so is inconsistent offensive play and coaching. The defense for L.A. has overcome missing Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Aaron Donald, Nate Landman and more, but the defense for the Rams has been objectively better than their offense this year. In Week 9, the Rams failed to convert a third down until the second half. The offense had Nacua on the field. Trade or not, the offense needs to be better. The Rams chose to go into 2026 with this receiving group Though it would be financially tough , the Rams could make a trade or add someone new. Just because they could, doesn’t mean they should. And if they do, there is no guarantee that it would work. They can’t trade for Nacua to save their season, and there is no recreating Nacua in the aggregate . The Rams have options, but none of them may be able to help the Rams enough in 2026 to play past Week 18. The Rams had the entire offseason to seriously revamp or retool their receiver room. They didn’t. Was that a feature or a glitch? Due to injuries to Nacua, Adams and even Terrence Ferguson, L.A.‘s passing game has been glitching, but the Rams went into this year thinking their pass catchers were a feature. At this point in the season, it may be too late for a trade to patch it. The Rams may just have to play better with who they have.

stories.title: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh says X-rays on QB Justin Herbert's finger negative
stories.summary: X-rays on the injured middle finger of Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert's left hand came back negative for a fracture, coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday.
stories.detailText: X-rays on the injured middle finger of Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert 's left (non-throwing) hand came back negative for a fracture, coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday. "The imaging came back negative, so he should be good to go," Harbaugh told reporters. Herbert left Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans in the fourth quarter because of his injury. Herbert said Sunday he wanted to stay in the game, but Harbaugh said Sunday he made the decision to keep him on the sidelines. Herbert was sacked a career-high eight times Sunday and threw his 11th interception, tying him with New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye for the NFL lead. Before he exited the game, Herbert connected with Quentin Johnston on a 58-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter that ended a TD dry spell for the Chargers that lasted nearly a month. The Chargers (0-8) went 12 straight quarters and 37 offensive drives without a touchdown dating to Oct. 11. It was the most consecutive drives without a touchdown since the 2024 Miami Dolphins went 30 straight drives without reaching the end zone. The record is held by the 2000 Baltimore Ravens , who went 61 drives without a touchdown. With the touchdown drought over, the Chargers must turn their attention to ending another streak. They have lost 11 consecutive games dating to last season, the franchise's longest losing streak since they started 0-11 in 2000. The Chargers travel to face the Ravens (4-5) on "Monday Night Football" in Week 10 before returning home to face the New York Jets (2-7) in Week 11. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.title: Jake Ferguson, Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks for Cowboys
stories.summary: The Cowboys will play "multiple weeks" without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and backup running back Tyler Goodson, coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday.
stories.detailText: The Cowboys will play "multiple weeks" without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and backup running back Tyler Goodson, coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday. Ferguson sprained the posterior cruciate and the medial collateral ligaments in his left knee in the third quarter Sunday, and Goodson injured his knee in the second quarter but played through it into the second half. Goodson had a career-high 77 yards on 12 carries against the Colts. "A lot of these guys, they play on adrenaline, and this is a guy that has been incredible for us really the last two weeks," Schottenheimer said, via Todd Archer of ESPN. "And these guys, they want to tough it out. They care. They want to win. They want to do whatever it takes. And just doing some more exams and scans and things like that, a few things showed up that we'll keep an eye [out] for." Ferguson is second on the team with four touchdown catches. The Cowboys have only one slot remaining on the injured reserve designated-to-return list, having already designated seven players. "We're working through it," Schottenheimer said. Tight end Luke Schoonmaker has missed the past two games with a groin injury but will return this week, Schottenheimer said. Fullback Hunter Luepke is the only player behind starting running back Javonte Williams on the active roster. Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin are on the practice squad. "There's a lot of different ways to do it," Schottenheimer said of the running back situation. "I have a lot of confidence in Izzy. We'll be looking at a lot of different potential moves that we can make, but I'm not going to pretend that losing Goody doesn't affect us. The guy's been playing great football."

stories.title: Bears vs. Bucs Game Balls: Some How, Some Way
stories.summary: After an uneven victory over the Tampa Bay Bucs, @ryandroste hands out his Chicago #Bears Week 9 game balls.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears carries the ball past Tykee Smith #23 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and scores a touchdown during the first quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears walked away from Sunday Night Football this week with their seventh win of the season (and first on Sunday night since 2018). And yet, many fans went to bed on Sunday evening with some uneasiness about their favorite football team. Caleb Williams, after a masterful start in the first quarter, ended up having his worst game as a pro. Rome Odunze once again had a case of the drops. And the Bears suffered more injuries that left some big question marks moving forward. Bears fans are in a very different place as a fan base than they were a couple of years ago when most would have done just about anything for a win on prime time, no matter how it came about. These days, if a win isn’t dominant enough, some sections of the fan base are calling for heads. That is to say, expectations have risen. But even though some (many) things were undoubtedly sloppy in this week’s game against the Bucs, the Bears never trailed and Williams delivered a game winning drive in crunch time when the team demanded it most. Let’s just hope this is an experience that results in growth down the stretch. Let’s get to the game balls. Offense Game Ball: WR Luther Burden III Burden suffered a concussion near the end of regulation when he took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Rueben Bain Jr. along the sideline. The hit caused Burden to drop the ball, resulting in a turnover that led to the Bucs tying the game with a touchdown and successful two-point conversion. While the result of the play was costly, I’m not sure there’s a player in the league that could have taken that hit and not dropped the ball. And there’s certainly an argument to be made that the hit should have resulted in a flag, whether the helmet-to-helmet hit was intentional or not. But I digress. Prior to this play, Burden was once again the Bears’ number one and most reliable receiver throughout the game. He had seven catches for 97 yards and one touchdown. Burden’s 56-yard touchdown was the Bears’ second of the night and a beautiful sight, including a couple of broken tackles. At this point, it appeared the Bears were going to run the Bucs out of the stadium. Caleb Williams to Luther Burden III for a 56-yard touchdown 🙌 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zXsKY9tZ2H — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 Even though the Bucs would end up coming back, and credit to their defense for forcing several turnovers, Burden was the steady hand throughout most of the night on the offensive side of the ball. Defense Game Ball: LB Devin Bush Much has been written about Jeffery Simmons serving as a “multiplier” for a defense, and Bush has been one of the largest benefactors of said multiplication here in Chicago. With Simmons drawing double teams and attention up front, there is less of an opportunity for blockers to get to the second level and get their hands on Bears linebackers. This has led to Bush being able to utilize his top notch speed and become a real weapon on defense. That was certainly the case on Sunday night. Bush ended the night with 9 tackles, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Devin Bush hit pic.twitter.com/wXZgsXveya — ✶Ⓜ️𝕒𝕣𝕔𝕦𝕤 ▶️✶ (@_MarcusD3_) November 9, 2026 Devin Bush's speed on this TFL 😮‍💨 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MY7ucqU8U0 — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 The pick is no problem because Devin Bush just blew up this 4th down attempt from Bucs. Bears are back in business already in great field position. pic.twitter.com/iW2OHo9vGl — Ross Pins (@chisportsross) November 9, 2026 Honorable mentions on defense: DT Jeffery Simmons, DE Austin Booker, CB Jaylon Johnson, and CB Cam Lewis. This one really was a close call this week. Booker would have likely been my next choice. Who would have received your game balls? Let us know in the comments section below.

stories.detailText: Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert underwent imaging on his injured left middle finger, and coach Jim Harbaugh said the tests came back negative for a fracture. stories.title: Sources: Cardinals' Gardner Minshew has UCL injury; Michael Wilson out for year
stories.summary: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew probably will need season-ending surgery on his right UCL, sources told ESPN. Michael Wilson, Arizona's top wide receiver, is also out for the season because of a neck injury.
stories.detailText: TEMPE, Ariz. -- The Cardinals ' offense took two major blows Monday. Quarterback Gardner Minshew II probably needs season-ending surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament, sources told ESPN, and wide receiver Michael Wilson will sit out the rest of the season because of a neck injury, coach Mike LaFleur said. Sources told ESPN that Minshew is seeking additional medical opinions to confirm whether he'll need the UCL surgery. Minshew was injured on a hit on the last play of the first half from Seattle Seahawks linebacker Dante Fowler Jr . Fowler hit Minshew as he was throwing, forcing a fumble. Minshew appeared to be in pain on the ground and then as he walked off to the locker room at the intermission but continued to play for the rest of the game. With Minshew expected to be out, the Cardinals are set to turn to rookie quarterback Carson Beck on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams . The team also plans to sign veteran Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals ' practice squad, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. A source told ESPN that Wilson fractured a vertebra and was expected to be in a brace for the next six weeks to two months. LaFleur said he's not worried about Wilson's injury being long term. The injury happened on the Cardinals' fourth offensive play when Wilson hauled in a 17-yard pass from Minshew and was then tackled by Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon . Wilson landed on his head but only told the Cardinals that he had a kink in his neck. "He's such a warrior that he didn't think much of it," LaFleur said. "And then obviously when the adrenaline wore down and he got his test today, that's when we knew." Wilson finishes his season with 546 yards and two touchdowns on 51 catches. He was on pace for his second straight 1,000-yard season. Wilson signed a three-year extension in September worth $75 million, with $47 million guaranteed. Wilson is the latest Cardinals receiver to be lost. After trading Marvin Harrison Jr . to the Houston Texans in Week 5, the Cardinals lost Jalen Brooks and Kendrick Bourne for the season because of wrist and ankle injuries, respectively. Arizona is now down to Simi Fehoko , Devin Duvernay , Reggie Virgil and Harrison Wallace III as its only active receivers. Recently signed receivers Zay Jones , Shedrick Jackson and James Proche II are currently on the practice squad. LaFleur said he has never experienced as many injuries at a single position as he has this season. During a team meeting Monday, LaFleur said he told his players that there is "a lot of opportunity" after all the injuries. "A lot of opportunity for guys to go out there and show us what they got," LaFleur said. "So, where there's setbacks, there's setups for success. So, we'll go from there." Who will throw to the remaining receivers is also in limbo. Beck spent last week as the second-string quarterback following the first eight weeks as the emergency third. LaFleur said there won't be any major changes to the offense if Beck were to take it over. "Yeah, I mean it's not like it's the difference between a wing-T offense and a spread offense," LaFleur said. "Foundationally, we're going to do a lot of the similar stuff and a lot of the stuff that Carson likes and is good at is the same stuff that Gardner likes. They like this system, and so that's not a hard one."

stories.title: Game Recap: Saints host Browns in Week 9 clash
stories.summary: Catch up on all the Saints action from Sunday.
stories.detailText: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints runs the ball against Ronnie Hickman #33 of the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Caesars Superdome on November 08, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints were back in action after the bye week when the Cleveland Browns visited the Big Easy on Sunday afternoon. Here’s a full recap of the matchup. First Quarter Cleveland began the game by going three-and-out, before Audric Estime got the Saints offense going straight away with three runs totalling 32 yards. Tyler Shough then found Juwan Johnson for 19 more with his first throw, but a few unsuccessful runs and a sack later, the Saints were held to a field goal attempt. Charlie Smyth converted from 30 yards to give the black and gold an early lead. The Browns were then forced into another quick punt as the Saints defense got off to a strong start. Shough found Chris Olave for 11 yards before breaking off for a 14-yard run, but it was soon another field goal attempt after he was sacked on 3rd down. This time, Smyth was no good from 52 yards, and the score remained 3-0. Second Quarter Shadeur Sanders found the first big play of the game for Cleveland with a 16-yard pass to Dylan Sampson, who also had a few short gains on the ground as the Browns drove past midfield. After being stuffed short of the chains on 3rd down, a 41-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt tied the game. Shough then copied a play from Paris with a 52-yard bomb downfield to Barion Brown as the Saints sought to regain the lead. But a play later, Jordyn Tyson fumbled after making a catch, which the defense fell on to return possession to the Browns. New Orleans was able to force another quick punt out of the Browns, but Brown fumbled on the return. Cleveland fell on it in the red zone. A penalty against Carl Granderson helped the visitors set up 1st-and-goal, but he made up for it by sacking Sanders to push them back. A few plays later, Sanders was just short of the goal line on 3rd-and-goal. The Browns offense stayed out there, and the Saints were able to come out big with a stop on 4th down to keep the game at 3-3. Shough connected with Olave for 36 yards to move the Saints out from deep in their own territory, but after another pass for just one yard and two incompletions, they were forced to punt just before the half. Third Quarter New Orleans went three-and-out and punted to begin the second half, before Sanders scrambled for 11 yards on 3rd down to avoid the same fate. He then completed a 60-yard pass to Denzel Boston to set up 1st-and-goal. But the Saints’ defense came up huge once again, with a tackle-for-loss, sack, and incompletion from Sanders limiting Cleveland to a chip-shot field goal that gave them a 6-3 lead. Shough responded with a scoring drive of his own, on a 54-yard drive highlighted by a 12-yard pass to Noah Fant and his own scrambles moving the ball down the field. Smyth’s 27-yard kick tied the game at 6-6. Cleveland then went three-and-out as Granderson got to the quarterback once again, but New Orleans would do the same, which gave the visitors the ball to begin the fourth. Fourth Quarter Sanders got the ball to midfield with a 10-yard pass to KC Concepcion, but failed to find another first down. He threw an incomplete pass to Sampson on 4th-and-2, and the Saints took over on downs again. Taking advantage of the shorter field, Shough moved the black and gold into field goal range with a 9-yard throw to Tyson. After being sacked by Myles Harden, the Saints were forced into yet another field goal, which Smyth converted from 48 yards. But the lead didn’t last long, as Sanders threw a 64-yard touchdown to Concepcion on the opening play of the ensuing drive to give Cleveland a 13-9 advantage. New Orleans then went three-and-out, before Cleveland had another punt of their own around the two-minute warning. Needing a touchdown, Shough found Olave for 33 yards to move the drive into the red zone. He then found Alvin Kamara for 8 more, before Estime ran in the 2-yard score to re-establish the lead for the black and gold. But Sanders threw twice for a total of 37 yards to Jerry Jeudy, which set up a field goal that Szmyt converted from 51 yards to force overtime. Overtime The Saints received first, and Kamara broke off three big runs as the ball moved past midfield. Shough then found Devaughn Vele for 9 yards before Estime ran for 9 more. Shough ran for 8 yards before finding Vele again, setting up a 15-yard touchdown throw to Johnson to give the black and gold a 23-16 lead. Needing a touchdown of their own, two passes from Sanders to Boston helped Cleveland into Saints territory. Sanders then found Harold Fannin Jr for a 39-yard touchdown. Cleveland opted to go for two and the win, which is where the Saints came up with the biggest stop of the day as Sanders’ pass intended for Boston fell incomplete. New Orleans held on 23-22 to set up a huge divisional matchup next weekend with the Carolina Panthers.

stories.title: Vikings sign former Giants star to active roster ahead of 'Monday Night Football'
stories.summary: Will Odell Beckham Jr. play tonight? The Minnesota Vikings could give the former Giants star a shot on "Monday Night Football."
stories.detailText: Odell Beckham Jr. hasn't recorded a catch since 2024. Could the Week 9 " Monday Night Football " game be his chance to get back in the box score? The Minnesota Vikings signed the veteran wideout to their active roster from their practice squad on Monday, Nov. 9, ahead of their prime-time clash with the Buffalo Bills . Beckham is in line to make his debut in the game just over a month after he signed with Minnesota's practice squad on Oct. 7. Beckham, 34, did not play during the 2025 season but already made his NFL comeback earlier this year. In June, he re-signed with the New York Giants for a second stint and made the team out of training camp. BILLS VS VIKINGS: Live updates, score and more from 'Monday Night Football' The former first-round pick played 20 snaps across three games for Big Blue to begin the regular season. He did not record a catch on his lone target in those appearances, and the Giants waived Beckham at the end of September. The Vikings signed him shortly after his release from the Giants to add depth at wide receiver. With Jauan Jennings missing from "Monday Night Football" due to a calf injury, Beckham is up with the active roster. He may get another crack at recording his first catch in two years on Nov. 9, depending on his snap count – and whether Week 9 starter Carson Wentz looks his way. stories.title: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
stories.summary: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.
stories.detailText: FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," according to coach Brian Schottenheimer. According to sources, Ferguson suffered sprained posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligaments in his left knee in the third quarter of Sunday's 27-23 win against the Indianapolis Colts . Goodson suffered a knee injury in the second quarter but managed to return in the second half. He finished with 12 carries for a career-high 77 yards. Ferguson, who is second on the team in touchdown catches (four), was hit awkwardly on an 11-yard catch and immediately grabbed at his knee. He remained on the sideline after getting the knee taped up but did not return. "A lot of these guys, they play on adrenaline, and this is a guy that has been incredible for us really the last two weeks," Schottenheimer said of Goodson. "And these guys, they want to tough it out. They care. They want to win. They want to do whatever it takes. And just doing some more exams and scans and things like that, a few things showed up that we'll keep an eye for." Complicating matters for the Cowboys is the fact they have just one slot remaining on their injured reserve/designated to return list, having put the designation on seven players. A player misses at least four games if he is placed on injured reserve/DTR. "We're working through it," Schottenheimer said. Tight end Luke Schoonmaker (groin) has missed the past two games, but he will be available this week to help alleviate Ferguson's absence, Schottenheimer said. The Cowboys have only fullback Hunter Luepke on the 53-man roster behind Javonte Williams , but Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin are on the practice squad. "There's a lot of different ways to do it," Schottenheimer said of the running back breakdowns. "I have a lot of confidence in Izzy. We'll be looking at a lot of different potential moves that we can make, but I'm not going to pretend that losing Goody doesn't affect us. The guy's been playing great football." Wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder, hamstring), cornerback Joey Porter Jr . (ankle) and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (back, hamstring) were inactive against the Colts, and Schottenheimer said they will follow a similar practice plan this week by being limited before a decision is made on their availability for the San Francisco 49ers . Safety P.J. Locke has been ruled out for this week after suffering a concussion for the second straight week. Wide receiver Jonathan Mingo was unable to finish the Colts game and his status is uncertain. Wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) will work into practice this week but has missed the past three games. "Busy week in the training room for us," Schottenheimer said.

stories.title: Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors: Vikings, Broncos, Packers among potential landing spots as deadline approaches
stories.summary: The Colts are open to trading Jonathan Taylor and several teams are reportedly interested.
stories.detailText: Jonathan Taylor is the talk of the town after the Colts shifted their stance on trading him. I'll be cataloging every trade rumor and update we get on the situation in this article, starting with a big update. 11/7 Update: The Ringer's Tom Pelissero believes Taylor is staying in Indy. The Colts are looking for a blockbuster haul and no team has made them an offer. This is by no means the end of the saga, but it's increasingly likely that the Colts' unreasonable ask for Taylor prices out all interested parties. Three days before the NFL trade deadline, the most likely destination for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor is … staying in Indianapolis. And only the type of blockbuster offer no team has made could pry him out. Trade info galore in The Sweep Insider Notebook: https://t.co/2WjDotrPhy pic.twitter.com/jh4Gu5UU1d — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 7, 2026 Minnesota Vikings The Vikings make too much sense. They have possibly the best defense in the NFL and a weak passing attack. Given that a superstar quarterback isn’t walking through the door anytime soon, they should be an old-school, ground-and-pound offense that complements the defense for low-scoring wins. They don’t have the horses for that in their backfield right now. Aaron Jones has had a solid season while averaging 4.2 yards per carry, but he can’t make it through a game without picking up a new injury. Jordan Mason , on the other hand, has missed time with an injury of his own and is plodding his way to 3.9 yards per attempt. Minnesota also has extra draft capital in 2027 via the Jonathan Greenard trade, which netted them the Eagles’ third-round pick. Some trade talk ahead of the NFL’s Tuesday Nov. 10 trade deadline: pic.twitter.com/KbVNl8ua33 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 1, 2026 Denver Broncos The Broncos were reportedly the team that nearly outbid the Texans for David Montgomery in the offseason. Jonah Coleman has emerged as a solid option for them, but RJ Harvey is on injured reserve and J.K. Dobbins —now relegated to backup duties—is averaging a dreary 3.3 yards per carry. Taylor would immediately take over as the workhorse back on a team that has failed to create a successful ground game for Sean Payton’s entire tenure as head coach. Local reporter Zac Stevens makes it sound like they are pushing hard to get a deal done. The Broncos want Jonathan Taylor, per @ZacStevens ️ "I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor. This could happen at any moment. You might not want to go to sleep Broncos Country." "The Broncos are going to try to pull this… pic.twitter.com/ixzuSTSsYy — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) November 2, 2026 New York Giants 11/8 Update: NFL insider Josina Anderson says that the Giants have pulled out of conversations to acquire Taylor. Things change quickly in the NFL, but this sounds fairly definitive. The #Patriots are still monitoring the market for pass rush help-at a bargain- by the Trade Deadline next Tuesday, I’m told… The #Giants cooled on acquiring #Colts RB Jonathan Taylor because of price. They resolved to move on a while ago leading into today’s game vs Philly.… — JosinaAnderson (@JosinaAnderson) November 8, 2026 11/9 Update: While the Giants are reportedly out of the Taylor trade talks, their offer has been revealed. They were reportedly willing to part ways with second- and fifth-round picks for Taylor . The Colts declined, though that was likely to continue fielding offers. This might be the best deal they get. It would not be surprising for the Colts to circle back on this offer ahead of tomorrow's deadline. Cam Skattebo ’s weird season makes the Taylor trade even more viable. He leads all running backs in fumbles and was benched after losing the ball in overtime versus the Commanders. Skattebo came back with a vengeance in Week 7 with a 17/124/1 rushing line, but he also went down with a hamstring injury at the end of the game. It held him out of Week 9's contest, though it looks like he will be back for Week 10. With his minor injury and Tyrone Tracy on IR, the Giants could view running back as a need regardless of the availability of Taylor. The fact that a superstar happens to be up for grabs is simply fortuitous timing. Green Bay Packers The Packers are the last of the big four teams routinely linked to Taylor, including by NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, who didn’t list the Seahawks or Bengals. Though that’s simply pulling from the ticker on his Sunday morning segment. From @NFLGameDay Morning: #Ravens great Ray Lewis spoke to the team on Friday; The #Colts have some big decisions ahead, centered around Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor. pic.twitter.com/avvh3cSGIu — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 1, 2026 11/9 Update: The Packers were already getting nothing out of their ground game, and now Jacobs is hurt. He has a fractured finger, though there's a chance he manages to play through it in Week 10. Still, Jacobs has been dreadfully inefficient this year and has ongoing legal troubles. #Packers HC Matt LaFleur opening statement on RB Josh Jacobs: "We're aware of the prior allegations on Josh. We're going to allow the NFL to do its process. But I would anticipate him being a member of us moving forward." pic.twitter.com/sY49oL0ZhM — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 2, 2026 The injury could be the nudge Green Bay needed to pull the trigger on Taylor. Cincinnati Bengals Schefter didn’t specifically mention the Bengals in his Sunday morning hit, but NFL insider Jordan Schultz has included them as a team to watch. As the #Colts continue to field trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor, sources say the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are among the teams that have checked in. The asking price is believed to be too high right now, but sources do believe a trade is leaning to… pic.twitter.com/48DGn6zRF3 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 1, 2026 Cincy’s rushing attack is struggling this year. They are 22nd in EPA per rush attempt and Chase Brown ranks 38th in yards after contact per carry. Samaje Perine is shockingly ahead of him in that metric, though he only ranks 30th. The Bengals’ defense has improved this year, but it’s not going to carry them to a title. Their path to hoisting the Lombardi Trophy ultimately runs through having the league’s best offense. Taylor would round out an offense that already has an unstoppable passing attack. Seattle Seahawks This destination continues to look less likely by the week. Schultz included Seattle in his list of teams interested in Taylor, but he’s in the minority of reporters in that regard. The Seahawks just got first-round pick Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from stints on IR. Seattle trusts Charbonnet to do the dirty work and doesn’t have much tape on Price because of the month he spent on injured reserve. It would be surprising for them to throw in the towel on Price after just four games. At 4-4, they might not feel confident in pushing their chips in for the 2026 season either. The Giants at -160 (61.5 percent) are considerably more likely to make the playoffs than Seattle at -138 (58 percent), if you take DraftKings’ numbers at face value. Seattle is undoubtedly a better offense when they have an elite running back to lean on. Given Sam Darnold ’s middling play this year, they are likely a team that benefits more than the average roster from a great running back. But their investment in Price and shaky start make a trade unlikely. Washington Commanders The Commanders stick out as a logical fit for Taylor, but reporters aren’t bringing them up at all, so I’ll keep this brief. Even at 2-4-1, they’re still in the hunt for the NFC East crown. Their Week 10 game versus the Giants will have a massive impact on their place in the standings. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt on IR, Kaytron Allen waived, Jeremy McNichols potentially done for the year with a foot injury, and Jerome Ford waived, almost every notable member of the backfield is out of the picture. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the last ones standing. For a team with a dynamic, dual-threat quarterback, the Commanders do not have a running back who can take advantage of the extra attention defenses pay to Jayden Daniels . The Commanders will likely do their due diligence regarding Taylor, but the lack of buzz connecting them to the trade talks likely means they’re not in the running. Indianapolis Colts It’s worth mentioning that the Colts aren’t obligated to trade Taylor. Their asking price of a CMC-level haul could price all potential partners out. In 2022, the 49ers traded second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks to the Carolina Panthers for running back Christian McCaffrey. The Colts would seek a similar compensation package from teams looking to acquire Jonathan Taylor. https://t.co/6U6bHcoA7S — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 1, 2026 Taylor is an elite runner, but McCaffrey’s abilities as a receiver haven’t been matched by anyone since Marshall Faulk. McCaffrey was also 26 when he was traded. Taylor is 27 and will turn 28 at the end of the regular season. There are enough interested parties and a desire to make this happen from the Colts’ end that I bet a deal gets done, but it’s not a foregone conclusion.

stories.title: Mike McCarthy: Steelers improved since last Bengals matchup
stories.summary: Pittsburgh’s coach says the team has grown ahead of a battle for first place in the AFC North.
stories.detailText: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers and Bengals will meet for the second time this season on Sunday — a game between two 6-2 teams that will end with one moving into sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The last time Pittsburgh played the Bengals, the Steelers won 30-27 at home on Sept. 27. And talking to the media on Monday, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he’d “like the outcome to be the same” when the two teams clash again in Week 10. However, McCarthy acknowledged things will be different this week. This time, the game will be in Cincinnati, and on Sunday Night Football instead of the 1 p.m. EST time slot. Pittsburgh will be without Roman Wilson and could still be missing Michael Pittman Jr. at the wide receiver poison. But Pittsburgh has also improved in the weeks between the Bengals matchups, the Steelers head coach said. “I think we’re playing differently than we were the first time around,” McCarthy said. “I think we’re better … I think we’re definitely performing better in the trenches. I think, offensively, our ball distribution is better.” The Week 3 Bengals game was Pittsburgh’s first with Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor on the starting offensive line. It was also Jaylen Warren’s first 100-yard game of the season. McCarthy also credited with the defense with taking “a big step.” “I think the pressure, particularly in the last game, is something that will serve us very well moving forward against anybody,” he said. The Steelers managed eight sacks against the Browns in their last game in Week 8. “I think teams change,” McCarthy said. “It’s not who you’re playing — it’s when you play them. It’s November football. I think our football team is starting to reflect that. I think that’s what’s most important.” McCarthy said he watched the Bengals’ Week 9 game, a 34-17 drubbing of the Falcons in Madrid, live over the Steelers’ bye week. He said Cincinnati “looked great” on offense, but pushed back on talking about how the Bengals have changed since Week 3. “I wouldn’t say ‘change,’” McCarthy said. “I think Joe (Burrow) is on top of his game. That was an impressive oﬀensive performance yesterday. They’re rolling. … I think that’s the whole thing, is just make sure we’re dialed in on how we want to play and in touch with the matchups, ball distribution. I think (Burrow’s) time clock — the way he distributes the football and the connection he has with his receivers — is top notch.” Burrow currently ranks second in the NFL in passing yards with 2,386. His 23 passing touchdowns are the most in the league. Cincinnati also has two receivers in the top 15 for receiving yardage in Tee Higgins (758, six touchdowns) and Ja’Marr Chase (647, seven touchdowns). McCarthy said it was “fair” to say that the Steelers have a better handle on their secondary since the last Bengals game, when Joey Porter Jr. was still on the roster although not playing. “We’ve played eight games now,” he said. “We’ve had a chance to go through game plans. We’ve had a chance to build game plans as a staﬀ and with our players. We’ve had game day sideline adjustments. So, I think you could really say that for the whole team, as far as where we are today compared to where we were when we played them the first time.” McCarthy stressed the importance of combating Burrow’s ability to stay on time in the pocket and negate a pass rush; the Steelers only logged one sack in Week 3. “I think we’re in a rotation now. We’re in a good rhythm,” McCarthy said of the Steelers’ pass rush, now tied for third in the NFL with 26 sacks. “I think that’s all part of it. … I love the way our veteran guys communicate with our coaches and the younger guys. I think Cam (Heyward) and T.J. (Watt), and just the level of communication, the things they see and the adjustments they’re making for pass rush and creating those opportunities. So, that’s where things become a half second quicker.” Even if the pressure doesn’t result in a sack, McCarthy said “the little things matter.” “The pressure, that’s the diﬀerence between hitting the arm of the quarterback or bull rushing the A-gap where the quarterback can’t step into the throw,” he said. “I just think we’re better today than we were back four or five weeks ago.”

teamStories.detailText: SEATTLE -- Quarterback Drew Lock 's stint as the Seattle Seahawks ' fill-in starter will last at least another week, coach Mike Macdonald said Monday. Macdonald told Seattle Sports 710-AM that the team got positive news on the oblique injury Lock suffered Sunday while quarterbacking the Seahawks to a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals . Lock was starting in place of Sam Darnold , who was sidelined with quad and rib injuries. The Seahawks (5-4) play the Raiders in Las Vegas this coming Sunday before their bye in Week 11. "Good exam for Drew," Macdonald said in Monday's interview. "He's dealing with an oblique. I think it's something we can manage and [have] him play in the game," Macdonald said. "Sam will be another week. So it'll be a similar plan to last week." Darnold suffered a cracked rib on the second play of Seattle's loss to the Chicago Bears last Monday night, then injured his quad near the end of the game. The Seahawks did not place him on injured reserve, and Macdonald has described his status as week-to-week. Darnold did not practice leading up to the Arizona game. Macdonald said in his afternoon news conference that it looks like Darnold might return after the Week 11 bye. "I think so, yeah," Macdonald said. "He's making progress. It's just, we're going to need some more time." Lock, meanwhile, has been listed as a limited participant on every injury report the Seahawks have released since the start of Week 6. He said Thursday was the only day last week that he threw in practice as the team tried to manage the elbow injury that had him inactive for Seattle's previous two games. Lock hurt his quad in the third quarter against Arizona, which required a trip to the medical tent but not force him to miss a snap. He finished 19 of 28 for 175 yards, a touchdown and zero sacks. His total QBR of 90.0 was his best in three games this season and third-best of his eight-year career. Macdonald said postgame that it appeared Lock's status for this week would be up in the air due to his oblique, though the quarterback later said he was confident he'd be able to play if his number was called. Lock has yet to turn the ball over while starting two games this season -- both against Arizona -- and playing most of a third. He's thrown five touchdown passes, completed 71.1% of his passes and has a Total QBR of 84.4 in those three games, which have all been Seattle wins. Darnold has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions in six games since he returned from the glute injury he suffered on the fifth play of the season opener against the New England Patriots . In those six games, Darnold has completed 60.3% of his passes with a Total QBR of 50.6. Darnold was one of six Seahawks starters who did not play against Arizona, along with left tackle Charles Cross , left guard Quenton Nelson , wide receiver Rashid Shaheed , defensive tackle Leonard Williams and outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu . Macdonald confirmed that Nelson, acquired in an Oct. 27 trade with the Indianapolis Colts , will miss the Raiders game as he recovers from a knee procedure Monday. Asked whether Nelson could also return after the bye, Macdonald reiterated that he is week-to-week and noted that the Seahawks' decision to not put him on injured reserve is an indication that they do not anticipate him missing four games. "I think we're optimistic on a bunch of guys, but we'll see how the week shakes out," Macdonald said.

Raiders' Klint Kubiak expresses confidence in DC Rob Leonard amid struggles
teamStories.summary: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak expressed confidence in first-time DC Rob Leonard after Las Vegas' sixth straight game of allowing 30-plus points.
teamStories.detailText: HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak does not anticipate any changes to the defense, expressing confidence in first-time defensive coordinator Rob Leonard after their 38-17 loss to the 49ers on Sunday -- the sixth straight game of allowing 30-plus points. "In fact, I see us doing the things we said we're going to do [but] better," Kubiak said Monday. "Stand behind, Rob. Stand behind our defensive staff. Stand behind our players. And I think the world wants someone's head on the platter every time things don't go right. But the way that I see it is that we brought people here for a reason: to get a job done and develop players for the long haul." Leonard's time as the defensive playcaller started with promise before turning into a complete disaster. During the Raiders' 3-0 start, they were eighth in points allowed (18 points per game), 11th in total yards allowed (316.7), second in EPA (22.65), third in defensive efficiency (75.96) and first in opponents' QBR (27). They were also tied for seventh in quarterback pressures (42), tied for fourth in sacks (10) and first in forced turnovers (9). The Raiders have lost five of six games since their 3-0 start, and the defense is a big reason for their struggles. Since Week 4, Las Vegas is near the bottom in every statistical category. They are last in points allowed (35.7 per game), rushing yards allowed (168.7) and defensive efficiency (17.54). Las Vegas is 17th in pressures (63) and tied for 29th in sacks (9). The Raiders have only recorded five turnovers during this stretch. In Week 9, San Francisco picked apart the Raiders in the pass and run game. Las Vegas gave up 190 rushing yards, including 94 in the first quarter. They had difficulty creating pressure on quarterback Brock Purdy , who completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Las Vegas gave up 414 total yards while the 49ers had possession for 38 minutes and 18 seconds. Despite the team's issues on defense, Kubiak still believes in the defensive scheme and the playcaller. "I have seen it work. Just not for four quarters," Kubiak said. "... As a group, it's putting four quarters of football together no matter who's the opponent. You play a damn good offense in San Francisco; there's got to be a happy medium somewhere between the first half and second half."

teamStories.summary: The 49ers and Raiders went toe to toe on the football field on Sunday, while the fans went at it off the field.
teamStories.detailText: The Raiders lost 38-17 to the 49ers Sunday. San Francisco hosted the team at Levi’s Stadium, where the Battle of the Bay rivalry was renewed. While the Raiders are no longer across the San Francisco Bay Bridge on the Oakland side, fans have shown there is still bad blood between franchises as things got violent from Santa Clara to Las Vegas. Raiders and Rams fans fight at the Fremont Street Experience in downtown Las Vegas. Instagram/@orlandoelectric2020 Raiders fans throwing hands in Las Vegas https://t.co/CelqntgObM — WORLDSTARHIPHOP (@WORLDSTAR) November 9, 2026 One Instagram user, @Orlandoelectric2020, captured several brawls breaking out on Fremont Street where several Raiders fans watched the game. One man was captured face down on the floor with a small pool of blood as a trio of three other men continued to throw hands in a wild scene. The Raiders relocated to Vegas in January 2020, but the fanbase evidently takes the rivalry with the 49ers seriously. So much so that some have resorted to violence. Had the Raiders won Sunday’s showdown, it doesn’t seem like the outcome would have made a difference as fights broke out before, during and after the game. Raiders and Rams fans fight during a brawl at the Fremont Street Experience in Downtown Las Vegas. Instagram/@orlandoelectric2020 Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer, middle, fumbles between San Francisco 49ers’ Ji’ayir Brown and Upton Stout on Nov. 8, 2026, in Santa Clara, Calif. AP Photo/Kelley L. Cox The video appeared to show Raiders fans fighting each other, and from the comments, potentially Rams fans as well. There did not appear to be any 49ers fans in the video that surfaced from Fremont Street. So, Raiders fans might have just been very angry after another deflating loss. But now, it’s clear the violence wasn’t contained to Levi’s Stadium, instead spreading all the way to Las Vegas.
